title_en: Alabama launches investigation into OpenAI’s hack of Hugging Face
title_fa: آلاباما تحقیقاتی را در مورد هک Hagging Face توسط OpenAI آغاز کرد
excerpt_en: Weeks after OpenAI disclosed that one of its cybersecurity models had gone rogue and hacked AI dataset company Hugging Face, Alabama’s attorney general announced an investigation into the incident.
excerpt_fa: Weeks after OpenAI disclosed that one of its cybersecurity models had gone rogue and hacked AI dataset company Hugging Face, Alabama’s attorney general announced an investigation into the incident.
content_en:
Alabama’s attorney general announced Monday that it sent a subpoena to OpenAI as part of an investigation into the company’s alleged “complete lack of oversight and adequate safeguards” in the Hugging Face incident.
The investigation comes weeks after OpenAI admitted that one of its unreleased and guardrail-free cybersecurity models had escaped an isolated environment, connected to the internet, and hacked AI dataset platform Hugging Face. As Reuters first reported, Hugging Face was only one of four victims of what was supposed to be “an internal evaluation” of a model with “maximal cyber capabilities,” as OpenAI put it.
The press release announcing the subpoena sent by the state’s attorney general Steve Marshall said that the state was seeking to understand if OpenAI’s “inability or unwillingness to ensure the safety of its products” violated the state’s consumer protection laws.
When reached by TechCrunch for comment, OpenAI spokesperson Nate Evans provided the statement: “The Hugging Face incident marked an important moment for AI safety and we are conducting a thorough review along with external advisors. Once the review is complete, we will share a technical report with relevant government authorities and publish our findings publicly.”
Earlier this month, Marshall, along with the attorneys general of 14 other states, including Florida, Missouri, Pennsylvania, and Texas, sent a letter to OpenAI’s CEO Sam Altman, requesting that he and his company preserve all records related to the Hugging Face incident. The letter also asked OpenAI to “immediately cease and desist” from any internal cybersecurity evaluations.
In the wake of the Hugging Face incident, and several other incidents disclosed by Anthropic, the U.K.’s AI Security Institute, Meta, and workers at AI companies — including executives and technical leaders — signed an open letter called “Pacing the Frontier,” which called for developing AI capabilities slowly and more responsibly. The letter also called for the U.S. government to support an “international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.”
Updated with comment from OpenAI.

title_en: Amazon hikes hardware prices by 60%, blaming memory shortage
title_fa: Amazon hikes hardware prices by 60%, blaming memory shortage
excerpt_en: As the memory shortage continues to cause trouble for hardware makers, Amazon says it is now being forced to pass on the costs to its consumers.
excerpt_fa: از آنجایی که کمبود حافظه همچنان برای سازندگان سخت‌افزار مشکل ایجاد می‌کند، آمازون می‌گوید اکنون مجبور است هزینه‌های آن را به مصرف‌کنندگان خود منتقل کند.
content_en:
Over the weekend, Amazon significantly raised the prices of its hardware devices, jacking them up by as much as 60% in some cases.
The price explosion impacted Fire TVs, Echos, Kindles, and Eeros. One egregious example that’s been cited is that of the Echo Dot, one of Amazon’s cheapest smart speakers, the price of which jumped 60% overnight, from $49.99 to $79.99. Price-tracking sites like CamelCamelCamel show the stark uptick, which has previously hovered much lower.
When reached for comment by TechCrunch, Amazon shared the following: “The consumer electronics industry is facing significant increases in memory and storage component costs. After absorbing these increases for as long as we could, we recently adjusted pricing across our product lines.”
The company also said that it would continue to offer occasional promotions to customers over the course of the next year.
Amazon’s price hikes reinforce the reality that it’s a terrible time to buy hardware. The global memory shortage fueled by the AI boom (also known as “RAMmageddon“) is driving up the cost of producing devices of all stripes. As a result, companies are increasingly passing on the costs to their customers.
In a sign of the times, Apple recently hiked its prices, and has sought to offset the steep new rates by introducing a device-leasing program, thus allowing users to pay off their devices over time.
The RAM shortage is expected to continue throughout 2027 before prices potentially crest and stabilize in 2028.

title_en: Amjad Masad, CEO and co-founder of Replit, joins the Disrupt Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
title_fa: امجد مساد، مدیر عامل و یکی از بنیانگذاران Replit، در TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 به Disrupt Stage می‌پیوندد.
excerpt_en: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, Replit CEO Amjad Masad will share his perspective on the future of programming and Replit's role in developing it.
excerpt_fa: در TechCrunch Disrupt 2026، امجد مساد، مدیر عامل Replit دیدگاه خود را در مورد آینده برنامه نویسی و نقش Replit در توسعه آن به اشتراک می گذارد.
content_en:
The AI boom has made it possible for a significantly wider range of people to dip into development, create code, and launch software for the first time. There are pros and cons to this, even for established developers who are being pushed to use it to produce work faster.
Replit sits at the center of this evolution, and when its CEO and co-founder, Amjad Masad, takes center stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, he’ll speak about the future of programming and the wide-ranging implications of a world in which ideas can be easily turned into products.
Join the audience to watch our wide-ranging discussion with Masad at San Francisco’s Moscone West from October 13–15. You’ll also catch the rest of our excellent Disrupt lineup across six stages that address the most pressing questions facing the startup community, including, most critically, how do you build a sustainable company in the AI era?
Get your tickets now during our special promotional pricing extension — get up to $300 off your ticket until 11:59 p.m. PT Tuesday, August 25.
Why Replit is joining the Disrupt Stage
Replit’s rise has been explosive, mirroring the broader ascent of AI and the companies furthering its proliferation. Though Masad founded the company a decade ago, the past 18 months have marked the biggest changes, with the company’s current run-rate tracking toward a billion dollars annually, compared with just $2.8 million in reported revenue in 2024.
But this conversation is about much more than Replit’s revenue. Masad’s conversation will dive into his perspective about the future of programming, entrepreneurship, and how Replit ensures that its service is doing more than helping users prototype their ideas — it helps fully flesh them out, too.
Investors are convinced of Replit’s value to both nontechnical users and professional coders. They assigned the company a $9 billion valuation earlier this year, a mere six months after the company was assigned a $3 billion valuation.
Of course, the question is whether it can keep that momentum going — or whether its growth in 2026 will look quaint a year from now because it’s growing even faster.
If you’re interested in building within the AI era, you can count on many sessions, in addition to Masad’s, across our other stages:
- Builders Stage, which will be chock-full of VCs and corporate development pros who’ll dive deep, providing the kinds of insights every founder needs to have.
- AI Stage, where we’ll examine the presumed SaaSpocalypse, career opportunities, emerging security challenges, and more.
- Smart Systems Stage, for those working on the vital infrastructure underpinning this era and for those who need to learn more about it.
- Real World AI Stage, where we’ll explore the sundry ways that new technologies are beginning to impact the physical world around us.
To hear it first and in person, join the more than 10,000 founders, investors, and technologists who are heading to San Francisco for Disrupt 2026 on October 13–15. Grab your ticket today to make sure you get the best available price.

رونق هوش مصنوعی این امکان را برای طیف وسیع تری از افراد فراهم کرده است تا برای اولین بار به توسعه، ایجاد کد و راه اندازی نرم افزار بپردازند. این مزایا و معایب دارد، حتی برای توسعه دهندگان معتبری که تحت فشار قرار می گیرند تا از آن برای تولید سریعتر کار استفاده کنند.
Replit در مرکز این تکامل قرار دارد و هنگامی که مدیر عامل و یکی از بنیانگذاران آن، امجد مساد، در مرکز TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 قرار می گیرد، در مورد آینده برنامه نویسی و پیامدهای گسترده جهانی که در آن ایده ها می توانند به راحتی به محصول تبدیل شوند، صحبت خواهد کرد.
برای تماشای گفتگوی گسترده ما با Masad در Moscone West سانفرانسیسکو از 13 تا 15 اکتبر به مخاطبان بپیوندید. شما همچنین می‌توانید بقیه خطوط عالی Disrupt ما را در شش مرحله مشاهده کنید که به فوری‌ترین سؤالات پیش روی جامعه استارت‌آپ‌ها پاسخ می‌دهد، از جمله مهم‌ترین آن، چگونه می‌توانید یک شرکت پایدار در عصر هوش مصنوعی بسازید؟
بلیط‌های خود را اکنون در طول افزایش قیمت‌های تبلیغاتی ویژه ما دریافت کنید - تا ساعت 11:59 بعد از ظهر تا 300 دلار از بلیط خود تخفیف بگیرید. PT سه شنبه، 25 اوت.
چرا Replit به مرحله Disrupt می پیوندد؟
ظهور Replit انفجاری بوده است، و منعکس کننده صعود گسترده تر هوش مصنوعی و شرکت هایی است که به گسترش آن کمک می کنند. اگرچه Masad این شرکت را یک دهه پیش تأسیس کرد، اما 18 ماه گذشته بزرگترین تغییرات را رقم زد، با ردیابی نرخ فعلی شرکت به یک میلیارد دلار در سال، در حالی که تنها 2.8 میلیون دلار درآمد گزارش شده در سال 2024 بود.
اما این گفتگو در مورد خیلی بیشتر از درآمد Replit است. مکالمه Masad به دیدگاه او در مورد آینده برنامه نویسی، کارآفرینی و اینکه چگونه Replit اطمینان می دهد که خدماتش بیشتر از کمک به کاربران برای نمونه سازی ایده های خود است، می پردازد - همچنین کمک می کند تا آنها را به طور کامل بیان کنند.
سرمایه گذاران از ارزش Replit هم برای کاربران غیر فنی و هم برای کدنویسان حرفه ای متقاعد شده اند. آنها در اوایل سال جاری، تنها شش ماه پس از تعیین ارزش 3 میلیارد دلاری شرکت، ارزش گذاری 9 میلیارد دلاری را به شرکت اختصاص دادند.
البته، سوال این است که آیا می‌تواند این شتاب را حفظ کند - یا اینکه رشد آن در سال 2026 یک سال بعد عجیب به نظر می‌رسد، زیرا حتی سریع‌تر هم رشد می‌کند.
اگر به ساختن در عصر هوش مصنوعی علاقه دارید، می‌توانید در مراحل دیگر ما علاوه بر جلسات Masad، روی جلسات زیادی حساب کنید:
- Builders Stage، که مملو از VCها و متخصصان توسعه شرکتی است که عمیقاً غوطه ور خواهند شد و انواع بینش هایی را که هر بنیانگذار باید داشته باشد ارائه می دهد.
- مرحله هوش مصنوعی، جایی که SaaSpocalypse فرضی، فرصت های شغلی، چالش های امنیتی در حال ظهور و موارد دیگر را بررسی خواهیم کرد.
- مرحله سیستم های هوشمند، برای کسانی که روی زیرساخت های حیاتی زیربنای این دوره کار می کنند و برای کسانی که نیاز به یادگیری بیشتر در مورد آن دارند.
- مرحله هوش مصنوعی دنیای واقعی، جایی که روش‌های مختلفی را که فناوری‌های جدید شروع به تأثیرگذاری بر دنیای فیزیکی اطراف ما کرده‌اند، بررسی می‌کنیم.
برای شنیدن آن ابتدا و شخصاً، به بیش از 10000 بنیان‌گذار، سرمایه‌گذار و فن‌آوری بپیوندید که در تاریخ 13 تا 15 اکتبر برای Disrupt 2026 به سانفرانسیسکو می‌روند. امروز بلیط خود را بگیرید تا مطمئن شوید که بهترین قیمت موجود را دریافت می کنید.

title_en: The cat-and-mouse game over 3D-printed guns has begun
title_fa: The cat-and-mouse game over 3D-printed guns has begun
excerpt_en: The creator of the world's first 3D-printed gun claims he's developed a way to thwart government-mandated software meant to block 3D printers from making firearms. It's an opening volley in what's shaping up to be an evolving battle between regulators trying to stem the tide of...
excerpt_fa: The creator of the world's first 3D-printed gun claims he's developed a way to thwart government-mandated software meant to block 3D printers from making firearms. It's an opening volley in what's shaping up to be an evolving battle between regulators trying to stem the tide of...
content_en:
The creator of the world’s first 3D-printed gun claims he’s developed a way to thwart government-mandated software meant to block 3D printers from making firearms. It’s an opening volley in what’s shaping up to be an evolving battle between regulators trying to stem the tide of ghost guns and individuals trying to create workarounds.
The cat-and-mouse game over 3D-printed guns has begun
The ‘Hochulization’ tool purports to subvert proposed gun-blocking 3D printer software.
The ‘Hochulization’ tool purports to subvert proposed gun-blocking 3D printer software.
Cody Wilson, who claims to have made the detection-defying tool, is calling it “Hochulization” as a direct jab at New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who pushed through the nation’s first law mandating gun file detection software on new printers earlier this year. “New York is trying to reach into the internet and police how open-source 3D printing is done,” Wilson, who’s based out of Austin, Texas, told The Verge. “I think of it as a self-defense measure.”
The tool is designed to break a relatively simple approach to a 3D-printed gun ban. Wilson’s company, Defense Distributed, runs DEFCAD, the world’s largest 3D gun file repository, which he says hosts over 200,000 files of gun designs and components, such as suppressors. Each of those files can be identified by a hash, a unique string of numbers that’s created by running the file through an algorithm. In theory, a gun file detection system that uses a hashing-based identification method would look for those exact hashes to determine whether a file is a potential gun, flag it, and prevent it from printing.
Hochulization mucks up that process by automatically changing those hashes. It adds a series of bytes to each file that changes the hash without altering the function of the end product. A 3D-printed suppressor or gun, in other words, would still work as intended. “Hochulizaiton is a de minimis policy to change the hash of every file that gets created and downloaded to where there is never going to be a complete library of hashes,” Wilson says.
Wilson says he wants to apply the Hochulization treatment to all files hosted on DEFCAD by default as a means of “self-defense” against growing calls for gun detection software, which he describes as invasive digital surveillance. Wilson says he will make the tool available to DEFCAD users, though he says he also intends to make it open source, which would let an individual user with a gun file apply the tool to scramble the hash and potentially sidestep detection.
“I think all the files in the repository, the 3D files anyway, should be Hochulized,” he adds. “And so that is what we’ll do.” He claims he has begun this process.
Wilson’s approach is an early indicator of the resistance to 3D-print-blocking tech. In this case, the momentum is coming from a Second Amendment advocate, but that might not always be the case. Groups of makers, digital rights experts, and members of the entertainment industry who aren’t focused on guns have all spoken out against the tech, expressing fears that requiring file scanning on printers introduces a new level of digital surveillance into the process that could limit what everyone can create.
3D-printed firearms are growing in number but remain an evolving public threat. In 2021, the New York Police Department confiscated just one 3D-printed gun. That jumped to 109 in 2024. Prominent gun policy group Everytown found similar upticks across 20 other cities. Still, when compared with the percentage of conventional firearms confiscated around the country, 3D-printed models remain comparatively small. The total number of firearms in the US has been estimated to outnumber people.
But 3D-printed gun technology has also come a long way since Wilson first printed his single-shot “Liberator” in 2013. Today, models like the FGC-9 can fire multiple high-velocity rounds without breaking and have been found in the hands of neo-Nazi cells in Europe and rebel groups fighting Myanmar’s military junta. 3D-printed gun components, like switches that can turn a single-fire conventional firearm into a machine gun or suppressors that make shots easier to conceal, are arguably even more dangerous. These tools are typically illegal or require special licenses to acquire. 3D printing offers a workaround. Luigi Mangione, who admitted to shooting and killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson and is awaiting sentencing, allegedly used a partially 3D-printed Glock-style pistol frame and a 3D-printed suppressor.
Policymakers and gun control advocates argue cases like this demonstrate a glaring gap in the legal system. People with prior felony convictions and others who aren’t legally allowed to own guns can do so anyway with the help of a 3D printer. And while many states regulate the making and selling of so-called “ghost guns,” actually enforcing those laws is notoriously difficult. This new approach, which requires 3D printers to install mandatory file-blocking software, attempts to close that gap by stopping a print before it ever starts. Industry experts are still debating whether that’s technically feasible at scale. Gov. Hochul, who pushed through the country’s first law mandating print-blocking software on new printers as part of the state’s FY 2027 budget, says it’s necessary to close what she calls a black-market “plastic pipeline.”
Hochul’s office did not respond to our request for comment regarding Wilson’s Hochulization workaround.
New York isn’t alone. A similar bill in California, AB 2047, is gaining momentum and is advancing to the Senate floor for a vote. Like in New York, this bill would require new printers manufactured or sold in the state to be equipped with print-blocking software. The state Department of Justice would publish a roster of compliant printer models, and those not on the list would be banned from sale or transfer in the state starting in December 2029.

اما فناوری اسلحه چاپ سه بعدی نیز از زمانی که ویلسون برای اولین بار در سال 2013 تک گلوله خود را چاپ کرد، راه درازی را طی کرده است. امروزه مدل هایی مانند FGC-9 می توانند چندین گلوله با سرعت بالا بدون شکستن شلیک کنند و در دست سلول های نئونازی در اروپا و گروه های شورشی که با حکومت نظامی میانمار می جنگند پیدا شده اند. اجزای اسلحه چاپ شده با چاپ سه بعدی، مانند سوئیچ هایی که می توانند یک اسلحه گرم معمولی تک شلیک را به یک مسلسل تبدیل کنند یا سرکوب کننده هایی که مخفی کردن شلیک را آسان تر می کنند، احتمالاً خطرناک تر هستند. این ابزارها معمولاً غیرقانونی هستند یا برای دستیابی به مجوزهای خاصی نیاز دارند. پرینت سه بعدی راه حلی را ارائه می دهد. لوئیجی مانژیونه که به تیراندازی و قتل مدیرعامل UnitedHealthcare برایان تامپسون اعتراف کرده و در انتظار صدور حکم است، ظاهراً از یک قاب تپانچه به سبک Glock با چاپ سه بعدی و یک سرکوبگر چاپ سه بعدی استفاده کرده است.
سیاستگذاران و طرفداران کنترل اسلحه استدلال می کنند که مواردی از این دست نشان دهنده شکاف آشکار در سیستم حقوقی است. افرادی که قبلاً محکومیت های جنایی دارند و افرادی که از نظر قانونی مجاز به داشتن اسلحه نیستند، می توانند به هر حال با کمک چاپگر سه بعدی این کار را انجام دهند. و در حالی که بسیاری از ایالت‌ها ساخت و فروش به اصطلاح «تفنگ‌های ارواح» را تنظیم می‌کنند، اجرای این قوانین بسیار دشوار است. این رویکرد جدید، که به چاپگرهای سه بعدی نیاز دارد تا نرم‌افزار اجباری مسدودکننده فایل را نصب کنند، سعی می‌کند این شکاف را با متوقف کردن چاپ قبل از شروع آن ببندد. کارشناسان صنعت هنوز در حال بحث هستند که آیا این از نظر فنی در مقیاس امکان پذیر است یا خیر. فرماندار هوچول، که اولین قانون کشور مبنی بر اجباری کردن نرم افزارهای مسدودکننده چاپ در چاپگرهای جدید را به عنوان بخشی از بودجه سال مالی 2027 ایالت به اجرا درآورد، می گوید که باید آنچه را که او «خط لوله پلاستیکی» در بازار سیاه می نامد، بسته شود.
دفتر Hochul به درخواست ما برای اظهار نظر در مورد راه حل Hochulization Wilson پاسخ نداد.
نیویورک تنها نیست لایحه مشابهی در کالیفرنیا، AB 2047، در حال افزایش است و برای رای گیری به مجلس سنا می رود. مانند نیویورک، این لایحه مستلزم آن است که چاپگرهای جدیدی که در ایالت تولید یا فروخته می‌شوند به نرم‌افزار مسدودکننده چاپ مجهز شوند. وزارت دادگستری ایالتی فهرستی از مدل های چاپگر منطبق را منتشر خواهد کرد و آنهایی که در لیست نیستند از دسامبر 2029 از فروش یا انتقال در ایالت منع خواهند شد.

title_en: Apply now to host a Side Event at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
title_fa: اکنون برای میزبانی یک رویداد جانبی در TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 درخواست دهید
excerpt_en: Apply before September 4 to be a part of the TechCrunch Disrupt community by hosting your own Side Event.
excerpt_fa: قبل از 4 سپتامبر درخواست دهید تا با میزبانی رویداد جانبی خود، بخشی از انجمن TechCrunch Disrupt باشید.
content_en:
We’re getting close to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026! In less than two months, more than 10,000 innovators, founders, investors, and industry leaders will gather in San Francisco. You can meet up with that community the week of TechCrunch Disrupt, which runs from October 13-15.
With our Disrupt Side Events program, you can bring people together anytime from October 10-16 for a custom event that gets promoted to Disrupt’s attendees. But time is running out — our deadline to apply for Side Events is September 4, so act now!
What are the benefits of a Side Event?
Hosting a Side Event puts you in control of how your community meets up, placing your brand front and center with the people who matter most. Whether you’re a VC looking to spark conversations, a company ready to showcase breakthrough innovation, or a community builder with something to say, this is your moment to:
- Engage directly with thousands of the sharpest minds in tech.
- Build authentic relationships with potential partners, investors, and collaborators.
- Own your narrative and showcase your expertise on your terms.
- Generate buzz that extends far beyond the event itself.
Approved Side Events are all promoted to Disrupt attendees and the rest of our audiences through the official Side Events calendar and marketing channels.
What Side Events can you host?
Anything that aligns with your vision is likely to be approved. Everything from industry roundtables and VC office hours to deep-dive workshops to intimate dinners and casual networking happy hours have succeeded at past Disrupt events.
The format is yours to design — we just ask that you bring the energy and make sure it’s open to both Disrupt attendees and the broader public. We recommend hosting events that take place in the evenings during Disrupt from October 13-15, as there’s less competition and more post-conference excitement to fuel meaningful conversations with undivided audiences.
How can I apply for a Side Event?
You can look at the application form here, but it’s helpful to have a few things locked in before starting the application process:
- Have a venue selected in the Bay Area — this is all about in-person experiences.
- Have a title, description, and venue prepared for the event.
- Double-check the Side Events Host Guide and the Side Event Host T&Cs.
If you have additional questions, we’re here to help! Just email our Side Events team and we’ll follow up to help.
We prioritize events that provide meaningful value to founders, investors, and the startup community, but aside from that, you know your community and ideal audience the best! There’s zero cost to apply and participate, so let’s hear your ideas.
Apply by September 4 to be a part of Disrupt
Apply now and tell us your vision, goals, and what you need logistically in your application, and we’ll handle the rest to give your team the support and exposure you need to make the most of the community and opportunity Disrupt brings to San Francisco and the Bay Area.

title_en: The only GameCube that could play CDs and DVDs is rarely found below $1,000 today
title_fa: The only GameCube that could play CDs and DVDs is rarely found below $1,000 today
excerpt_en: This isn't your run-of-the-mill GameCube, and its value has skyrocketed over the years. Here's what it did and how to identify it.
excerpt_fa: This isn't your run-of-the-mill GameCube, and its value has skyrocketed over the years. Here's what it did and how to identify it.
content_en:
The only GameCube that could play CDs and DVDs is rarely found below $1,000 today
This is one strange console.
One reason GameCube games hold their value so well today is that, compared to other Nintendo consoles, it wasn't exactly a hot seller. Why was that? Well, it's partly because the PS2 had what the GameCube didn't: a built-in DVD player. Out of that market pressure was born the Panasonic Q. While this oddball GameCube/DVD player hybrid barely got off the ground, its scarcity has led to a second life as a niche collector's item.
The Japan-only Panasonic SL-GC 10, widely known as the Panasonic Q, arrived in December 2001, three months after the Nintendo GameCube debuted in Japan. Looking less like a Nintendo console and more like a home-theater appliance, the Q had a reflective front panel, a backlit LCD and ports with a blue glow. If you want quintessential 2001 consumer electronics design, look no further.
The oddball pairing of Panasonic branding with Nintendo gaming stemmed from an existing relationship between the two companies. It turns out Panasonic's then-parent company, Matsushita (which is essentially Panasonic today), helped design the GameCube's optical miniDVD format. It seems likely Nintendo saw the gaping DVD hole in its console strategy and decided to roll the dice.
A GameCube for the DVD era
The Panasonic Q was a bizarre mashup. Its motorized disc tray accepted GameCube discs, DVDs and audio CDs. The company took the home theater part seriously. The Q had a Cinema mode for picture processing, along with audio features like Dolby Digital, DTS (Digital Theater Systems) for surround sound, Dialogue Enhancer and Bass Plus.
Those home theater features sure must have been nice for games like Super Mario Sunshine or Metroid Prime, right? Unfortunately, no. That's because the Q's home theater features were split off from the game console. Game audio was limited to the GameCube's standard analog connections. There was even a hardware button to manually switch between the two modes because it wouldn't change automatically based on the disc type. When it was time to switch, the system effectively powered down one side and restarted the other.
The Q also came with Panasonic-branded accessories reflecting the product's duality. There's a gray GameCube controller with Panasonic branding for games and a matching gray remote control for the DVD player. This wasn't so much a hybrid device as it was two distinct machines from two companies sharing the same chassis. Oh, early oughts, how we miss you.
Setting aside the exterior, the gaming half of the Q was no different from a standard GameCube. You could pop in Super Smash Bros. Melee or Mario Kart: Double Dash!! and have an identical experience to your friend with the regular version. It had the same controller ports, memory card slots and full compatibility with the GameCube library (although unmodified models were region-locked to Japan).
The weird industrial design did lead to one tradeoff: the GameCube's Game Boy Player didn't fit. The optional accessory, which let you play Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance games, lodged underneath Nintendo's system. But because the Q's base was different, Panasonic had to release a modified version of the Game Boy Player designed for its shiny, weird console.
Despite all of that effort, the Panasonic Q struggled to find an audience — mostly because it was damn expensive. It launched in Japan at ¥39,800 (roughly $313 at the time) — a lot of money for such an oddball product. Although that matches the PS2's Japanese launch price, Sony's console arrived nearly two years earlier, had already built a huge audience and made the DVD player a central selling point. Not to mention, you didn't have to reboot your console to switch between the two modes. Plenty of modded imported units made it overseas, but the Q never launched outside of Japan.
A rare piece of gaming history
And that brings us back to its collectible status today. Because of all that, there just aren't that many Panasonic Qs in the wild today. So when they do turn up on places like eBay, they can fetch a pretty penny. Loose consoles generally sell in the $1,200 to $1,300 range. Models with the original packaging and paperwork can surpass $2,000. It wasn't a legendary product, but for those who held on to one, it ended up being a good investment.
It's only fitting that one of the weirdest game consoles ever made also has one of the strangest stories: being more successful as a 2020s collector's item than it ever was as a consumer product.

درست است که یکی از عجیب‌ترین کنسول‌های بازی که تا به حال ساخته شده است، یکی از عجیب‌ترین داستان‌ها را نیز داشته باشد: موفق‌تر بودن به‌عنوان یک کالای کلکسیونر دهه 2020 از همیشه به عنوان یک محصول مصرفی.

title_en: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns
title_fa: Instinct’s powerful AI assistant is raising privacy and security concerns
excerpt_en: Early testers are raving about what Instinct can do, but some say the AI assistant’s sweeping access, broad terms and ability to act on users’ behalf come with uncomfortable trade-offs.
excerpt_fa: آزمایش‌کنندگان اولیه درباره کارهایی که Instinct می‌تواند انجام دهد هیجان زده می‌شوند، اما برخی می‌گویند دسترسی گسترده، شرایط گسترده و توانایی دستیار هوش مصنوعی برای اقدام از جانب کاربران با معاوضه‌های ناخوشایندی همراه است.
content_en:
Everyone is buzzing about Instinct, an AI personal assistant still in private access, not only for its incredible capabilities, but also for its potential privacy concerns. The agent, a veritable taskmaster, has been praised as feeling “like magic” and being one of the “most exciting launches” since OpenClaw. However, some testers have also raised concerns about the AI agent’s security model and its worrisome terms of service.
To be fair, Instinct is still in private testing for now, so these concerns haven’t yet scaled to the wider public at this time.
Created by a small team led by former Sierra research scientist Noah Shinn, San Francisco-based Instinct is operated by Spear Street Technology, per its terms and California business filings. It’s currently operating in stealth, per PitchBook.
The AI agent itself works by connecting to your applications and devices, including your email, messaging apps, calendar, and your device’s audio, location, screen, and more. You can text the agent or call it via text message or WhatsApp, asking it to perform various tasks for you, like booking your appointments and reservations, scheduling a ride to the airport, cleaning up your inbox, organizing important information, handling your shopping, finding you cheap flights, and much more.
Though Instinct is described by testers as outperforming their expectations, some have also raised concerns about the company’s approach to customer privacy and security. This raises a timely question: Are the trade-offs of giving AI this level of access and autonomy actually worth it?
For instance, several people are circulating screenshots from the company’s Terms of Service, which grant Instinct a broad “perpetual and irrevocable” license to “access, use, host, cache, store, reproduce, transmit, display, publish, distribute, and modify” any of the user’s materials, including for training its AI models. The terms also detail how Instinct can receive information from users’ devices, including screen captures, cursor movements, and keyboard inputs.
The terms also allow Instinct to enter into “agreements, commitments, or transactions” on users’ behalf, which would be binding.
One early adopter, Peter Yang, pointed out that Instinct would not delete his Gmail records when asked. (The team later fixed the problem by adding a tool for deleting external data in its settings, he said.)
Another person, Claire Vo, found that Instinct was still summarizing their inbox after disconnecting its access. When she asked Instinct what happened, the bot confirmed that the emails were stored in plain text for later searches.
Many others questioned the security model, too. One tester was a bit worried when they found that Instinct was able to pull a sign-up code from their email inbox to complete a particular task — in their case, booking a table at a restaurant via Resy. And Hello Patient co-founder Alex Cohen wrote that once he found out how easily Instinct could be phished, he deleted his account:
In addition, Moxxie Ventures founder Katie Jacobs Stanton shared that Instinct broke her trust when it sent an email on her behalf without first checking with her.
“We’re trading privacy and control for hyper-personalized AI tools (AI notetakers, personalized AI agents, etc), often without fully understanding the trade,” she remarked on X, summarizing the dilemma posed personal AI agents. “The more powerful these agents become, the more trust matters. Every successful action earns a little more trust. One unauthorized action can reset that trust to zero,” she said.
Michael Mignano, the founder of Anchor, which was acquired by Spotify, and now a GP at Union Square Ventures, noted that products like Instinct are going to “change modern security norms for consumers,” adding that “people will increasingly hand over passwords to 3p [third-party] apps, unaware of how or what they are storing for them.”
Interest in Instinct and personal AI has been growing since the arrival of OpenClaw, a personal AI assistant that became popular for its powerful capabilities, leading its founder to join OpenAI to help work on the next generation of personal agents. Another messaging-based assistant, Poke, also just exited to Cognition.
Amid the criticism, Instinct’s team hasn’t yet responded to anyone’s concerns or complaints on X, preferring to keep a low profile. (The bot itself identifies Luca Borletti, also formerly of Sierra, as being involved with the company, but that has not been confirmed.) TechCrunch has heard from multiple investors that Kleiner Perkins and Conviction have invested in the startup and those rounds have now closed.
Requests for comment sent to both the startup’s main email address and Shinn directly have not yet been returned.
content_fa:
همه در مورد Instinct، یک دستیار شخصی هوش مصنوعی که هنوز در دسترس خصوصی است، نه تنها به دلیل قابلیت های باورنکردنی اش، بلکه به خاطر نگرانی های بالقوه خود در مورد حفظ حریم خصوصی، سر و صدا می کنند. این عامل، یک مدیر واقعی، به عنوان احساس «شبیه جادو» و یکی از «هیجان‌انگیزترین راه‌اندازی‌ها» از زمان OpenClaw مورد ستایش قرار گرفته است. با این حال، برخی از آزمایش‌کنندگان نیز نگرانی‌هایی را در مورد مدل امنیتی عامل هوش مصنوعی و شرایط خدمات نگران‌کننده آن مطرح کرده‌اند.
انصافاً، Instinct در حال حاضر هنوز در تست خصوصی است، بنابراین این نگرانی ها در حال حاضر برای عموم گسترده تر نشده است.
Instinct مستقر در سانفرانسیسکو که توسط یک تیم کوچک به رهبری دانشمند تحقیقاتی سابق سیرا، نوآ شین، ایجاد شده است، طبق شرایط آن و پرونده های تجاری کالیفرنیا توسط فناوری خیابان اسپیر اداره می شود. در حال حاضر به صورت مخفیانه، به ازای PitchBook، کار می کند.
خود عامل هوش مصنوعی با اتصال به برنامه‌ها و دستگاه‌های شما، از جمله ایمیل، برنامه‌های پیام‌رسان، تقویم و صدا، مکان، صفحه نمایش و غیره دستگاه شما کار می‌کند. می‌توانید از طریق پیامک یا واتس‌اپ به نماینده پیام دهید یا با آن تماس بگیرید، از او بخواهید کارهای مختلفی را برای شما انجام دهد، مانند رزرو قرار و رزرو، برنامه‌ریزی سفر به فرودگاه، تمیز کردن صندوق ورودی‌تان، سازمان‌دهی اطلاعات مهم، رسیدگی به خرید، یافتن پروازهای ارزان‌قیمت برای شما، و موارد دیگر.
اگرچه Instinct توسط آزمایش‌کنندگان توصیف می‌شود که از انتظارات آن‌ها بهتر عمل می‌کند، برخی نیز نگرانی‌هایی را در مورد رویکرد این شرکت به حفظ حریم خصوصی و امنیت مشتریان مطرح کرده‌اند. این یک سوال به موقع ایجاد می کند: آیا معاوضه های ارائه این سطح از دسترسی و استقلال به هوش مصنوعی واقعا ارزشش را دارد؟
به عنوان مثال، چندین نفر در حال پخش اسکرین شات هایی از شرایط خدمات شرکت هستند که به Instinct یک مجوز گسترده «دائمی و غیرقابل فسخ» را برای «دسترسی، استفاده، میزبانی، حافظه پنهان، ذخیره، تولید، ارسال، نمایش، انتشار، توزیع، و اصلاح» هر یک از مطالب کاربر، از جمله برای آموزش مدل های هوش مصنوعی اعطا می کند. این شرایط همچنین نحوه دریافت اطلاعات Instinct را از دستگاه‌های کاربران، از جمله عکس‌برداری از صفحه، حرکات مکان‌نما، و ورودی‌های صفحه‌کلید نشان می‌دهد.
این شرایط همچنین به Instinct اجازه می‌دهد تا از طرف کاربران «توافق‌ها، تعهدات یا معاملات» را وارد کند که الزام‌آور است.
یکی از کاربران اولیه، پیتر یانگ، اشاره کرد که Instinct در صورت درخواست، سوابق جیمیل او را حذف نمی کند. (او گفت که تیم بعداً با افزودن ابزاری برای حذف داده های خارجی در تنظیمات خود مشکل را برطرف کرد.)
شخص دیگری، Claire Vo، متوجه شد که Instinct پس از قطع دسترسی صندوق ورودی خود، همچنان در حال خلاصه‌سازی است. وقتی او از Instinct پرسید که چه اتفاقی افتاده است، ربات تأیید کرد که ایمیل‌ها در متن ساده برای جستجوهای بعدی ذخیره شده‌اند.
بسیاری دیگر نیز مدل امنیتی را زیر سوال بردند. یک آزمایش‌کننده زمانی که متوجه شد Instinct می‌تواند یک کد ثبت‌نام را از صندوق ورودی ایمیل خود برای تکمیل یک کار خاص - در مورد آنها، رزرو میز در یک رستوران از طریق Resy - بیرون بکشد، کمی نگران شد. و الکس کوهن، یکی از بنیانگذاران Hello Patient نوشت که وقتی متوجه شد که Instinct چقدر راحت می‌تواند فیش شود، حساب خود را حذف کرد:
علاوه بر این، کیتی جاکوبز استنتون، بنیانگذار Moxxie Ventures به اشتراک گذاشت که Instinct وقتی از طرف او ایمیلی ارسال کرد بدون اینکه ابتدا با او چک شود، اعتماد او را شکست.
او در X با خلاصه کردن معضلی که عوامل هوش مصنوعی شخصی ایجاد می‌کند، گفت: «ما در حال معامله حریم خصوصی و کنترل با ابزارهای هوش مصنوعی بیش از حد شخصی (یادداشت‌نویس‌های هوش مصنوعی، عوامل هوش مصنوعی شخصی‌شده، و غیره) هستیم. او گفت: "هرچه این عوامل قدرتمندتر شوند، اعتماد اهمیت بیشتری دارد. هر اقدام موفق کمی اعتماد بیشتری به دست می آورد. یک اقدام غیرمجاز می تواند این اعتماد را به صفر برساند."
مایکل میگنانو، بنیانگذار Anchor، که توسط Spotify خریداری شد و اکنون یک پزشک عمومی در Union Square Ventures است، خاطرنشان کرد که محصولاتی مانند Instinct قرار است "هنجارهای امنیتی مدرن را برای مصرف کنندگان تغییر دهند" و افزود که "مردم به طور فزاینده ای رمزهای عبور را به برنامه های 3p [شخص ثالث] تحویل می دهند، بدون اینکه بدانند چگونه یا چه چیزی را برای آنها ذخیره می کنند."
علاقه به Instinct و هوش مصنوعی شخصی از زمان ورود OpenClaw، یک دستیار هوش مصنوعی شخصی که به دلیل قابلیت های قدرتمندش محبوب شد، افزایش یافته است و باعث شد تا بنیانگذار آن به OpenAI بپیوندد تا به کار بر روی نسل بعدی نمایندگان شخصی کمک کند. دستیار دیگر مبتنی بر پیام، Poke نیز به تازگی از Cognition خارج شده است.
در میان انتقادات، تیم Instinct هنوز به نگرانی‌ها یا شکایات کسی در مورد X پاسخ نداده است و ترجیح می‌دهد مشخصات خود را پایین نگه دارد. (خود ربات لوکا بورلتی را که قبلاً از سیرا نیز بوده است، به عنوان درگیر با این شرکت معرفی می کند، اما تایید نشده است.) TechCrunch از چندین سرمایه گذار شنیده است که Kleiner Perkins و Conviction در استارتاپ سرمایه گذاری کرده اند و این دورها اکنون بسته شده اند.
درخواست‌های ارسال نظر به آدرس ایمیل اصلی استارت‌آپ و مستقیماً به Shinn هنوز برگردانده نشده‌اند.

title_en: CDPR is aiming to release The Witcher 4 in 2028
title_fa: CDPR is aiming to release The Witcher 4 in 2028
excerpt_en: CDPR's co-CEO called The Witcher 4"our biggest, boldest and most ambitious game to date."
excerpt_fa: CDPR's co-CEO called The Witcher 4"our biggest, boldest and most ambitious game to date."
content_en:
CDPR is aiming to release The Witcher 4 in 2028
"This is our biggest, boldest and most ambitious game to date."
CD Projekt Red (CDPR) joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski just revealed that the company is hoping to release The Witcher 4 in 2028. The long-awaited sequel was first announced all the way back in 2022, but didn't get a reveal trailer until The Game Awards in late 2024.
"Simply put, this is our biggest, boldest and most ambitious game to date," he said in a short video posted to social media. "I know it's a bit of a wait and you'd love to play it sooner, but let the team cook."
To our beloved fans, players, and community:
As we near #gamescom in just a few days, CD PROJEKT RED Joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski would like to personally invite YOU to join us there, and hear about the future of The Witcher franchise!
To that end, Nowakowski confirmed that CDPR will not be showing off the sequel at Gamescom, which starts on August 26. It will, however, be showing a whole lot of the upcoming The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past expansion. This is the third real-deal expansion for the 2015 action RPG and comes a full decade after the second one.
The company will reveal "a lot of the expansion" at Gamescom, including a "taste of its dark story and the new content it will bring." It's due sometime in 2027.
I, for one, am happy giving CDPR all the time it needs to make sure The Witcher 4 is as good as it can be on launch day. We all remember what happened with the original launch of Cyberpunk 2077.

title_en: How to add Bluetooth to a TV that doesn't have it
title_fa: چگونه بلوتوث را به تلویزیونی که آن را ندارد اضافه کنیم؟
excerpt_en: Your TV may not have native Bluetooth support, but you can still stream your TV's audio to wireless headphones.
excerpt_fa: Your TV may not have native Bluetooth support, but you can still stream your TV's audio to wireless headphones.
content_en:
How to add Bluetooth to a TV that doesn't have it
Look, we're all tired of hearing your shows echo through the house.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
With the right audio upgrades and a streaming device that unlocks the world of on-demand content, most televisions can last a very long time. Of course, there are certain upgrades that are harder to ignore — wireless connectivity being one of them. Bluetooth has become mainstream in most televisions now, with many infrared remote controls relying on the technology too. If you've purchased your TV in the past decade, there's a good chance it comes with Bluetooth support. Head to the settings menu and look for connectivity options that mention Bluetooth, wireless devices or accessories.
If you do own a television without support for Bluetooth, you're not necessarily out of luck. Pretty much all popular streaming devices, like the Apple TV, Roku or Fire TV Stick, feature Bluetooth as a standard feature. If you own a pair of wireless headphones or a keyboard, you can connect them directly to the streaming device. At $30, the Roku Streaming Stick HD is one of the most affordable ways to not just add Bluetooth support to your TV but also breathe some new life into it with a modern OS.
The only big downside of going the streaming device route is that your Bluetooth accessories will only work when your TV is set to that particular input source. If you switch back to any other device that's also connected to your TV, the sound will once again play from the TV's speakers. If you're looking for a more universal solution, picking up a dedicated Bluetooth transmitter is the better option.
How does a Bluetooth transmitter work?
Bluetooth transmitters do exactly what you'd expect — they carry over the audio from a device that doesn't have native Bluetooth support to a pair of wireless headphones or earbuds. The setup process is relatively straightforward. You plug the Bluetooth transmitter into your TV's audio output, put both the transmitter and your headphones into pairing mode, and wait for them to connect. Your TV then feeds its audio signal into the transmitter, which converts it into a Bluetooth signal that your headphones receive.
Depending on your TV model, you can find Bluetooth transmitters that accept audio through the optical port, a 3.5mm headphone jack or RCA outputs. You'll also need to plug the adapter into a power source — an available USB port on your TV usually does the job. You can find these adapters at various price points online, with decent options at around $25.
Look for transmitters that come with newer codecs like aptX Low Latency, which can help reduce the delay between what's happening on screen and what you hear through your headphones.
content_fa:
چگونه بلوتوث را به تلویزیونی که آن را ندارد اضافه کنیم؟
ببینید، همه ما از شنیدن صدای پخش برنامه های شما در خانه خسته شده ایم.
ممکن است بابت خریدهای انجام شده از پیوندها کمیسیون دریافت کنیم.
با ارتقاهای صوتی مناسب و دستگاه پخش جریانی که دنیای محتوای درخواستی را باز می کند، اکثر تلویزیون ها می توانند مدت زمان زیادی دوام بیاورند. البته، برخی به‌روزرسانی‌ها وجود دارند که نادیده گرفتن آنها سخت‌تر است - اتصال بی‌سیم یکی از آنهاست. بلوتوث در حال حاضر در اکثر تلویزیون ها به جریان اصلی تبدیل شده است و بسیاری از کنترل های مادون قرمز نیز به این فناوری تکیه می کنند. اگر تلویزیون خود را در دهه گذشته خریداری کرده اید، احتمال زیادی وجود دارد که از بلوتوث پشتیبانی کند. به منوی تنظیمات بروید و به دنبال گزینه‌های اتصالی باشید که به بلوتوث، دستگاه‌های بی‌سیم یا لوازم جانبی اشاره می‌کنند.
اگر تلویزیون بدون پشتیبانی از بلوتوث دارید، لزوماً خوش شانس نیستید. تقریباً همه دستگاه های پخش جریانی محبوب، مانند Apple TV، Roku یا Fire TV Stick، از بلوتوث به عنوان یک ویژگی استاندارد استفاده می کنند. اگر یک جفت هدفون بی سیم یا یک صفحه کلید دارید، می توانید آنها را مستقیماً به دستگاه پخش وصل کنید. Roku Streaming Stick HD با قیمت 30 دلار یکی از مقرون به صرفه ترین راه ها است که نه تنها پشتیبانی بلوتوث را به تلویزیون خود اضافه می کند، بلکه با یک سیستم عامل مدرن، جان تازه ای به آن می بخشد.
تنها نقطه ضعف بزرگ رفتن به مسیر دستگاه پخش جریانی این است که لوازم جانبی بلوتوث شما تنها زمانی کار می کنند که تلویزیون شما روی آن منبع ورودی خاص تنظیم شده باشد. اگر به دستگاه دیگری که به تلویزیون شما نیز متصل است برگردید، صدا دوباره از بلندگوهای تلویزیون پخش می شود. اگر به دنبال راه حل جهانی تر هستید، انتخاب یک فرستنده بلوتوث اختصاصی گزینه بهتری است.
فرستنده بلوتوث چگونه کار می کند؟
فرستنده‌های بلوتوث دقیقاً همان کاری را انجام می‌دهند که انتظار دارید - آنها صدا را از دستگاهی که پشتیبانی از بلوتوث بومی ندارد به یک جفت هدفون یا هدفون بی‌سیم منتقل می‌کنند. فرآیند راه اندازی نسبتاً ساده است. فرستنده بلوتوث را به خروجی صدای تلویزیون وصل می‌کنید، فرستنده و هدفون را در حالت جفت قرار می‌دهید و منتظر می‌شوید تا متصل شوند. سپس تلویزیون شما سیگنال صوتی خود را به فرستنده می رساند که آن را به سیگنال بلوتوثی تبدیل می کند که هدفون شما دریافت می کند.
بسته به مدل تلویزیون خود، می‌توانید فرستنده‌های بلوتوثی را پیدا کنید که صدا را از طریق درگاه نوری، جک 3.5 میلی‌متری هدفون یا خروجی‌های RCA می‌پذیرند. همچنین باید آداپتور را به منبع برق وصل کنید - معمولاً یک پورت USB موجود در تلویزیون شما این کار را انجام می دهد. شما می توانید این آداپتورها را با قیمت های مختلف آنلاین، با گزینه های مناسب در حدود 25 دلار پیدا کنید.
به دنبال فرستنده‌هایی باشید که دارای کدک‌های جدیدتر مانند aptX Low Latency هستند، که می‌تواند به کاهش تأخیر بین آنچه روی صفحه اتفاق می‌افتد و آنچه از طریق هدفون می‌شنوید کمک کند.

title_en: How to cancel your ChatGPT subscription (and why you might want to)
title_fa: How to cancel your ChatGPT subscription (and why you might want to)
excerpt_en: If you've had it with OpenAI, here's how to cancel your subscription and delete your account.
excerpt_fa: If you've had it with OpenAI, here's how to cancel your subscription and delete your account.
content_en:
How to cancel your ChatGPT subscription (and why you might want to)
If you want to cancel your subscription, you'll need to go through the same payment system you used to sign up.
Canceling a ChatGPT subscription only takes a few clicks. But if your goal is to quit ChatGPT entirely, stopping the recurring charge may be only one part of it. You might also want to delete your account, keep new chats out of model training or simply stop paying for features you no longer use. Canceling the subscription handles only the billing, so the right next step depends on what you actually want to stop.
Reasons to reconsider a paid ChatGPT plan
A paid plan makes the most sense when you regularly run into the Free tier's limits or rely on tools reserved for higher tiers. If that's no longer true, paying every month gets harder to justify. One option is ChatGPT Go, a lower-cost paid tier that OpenAI now offers in every country where ChatGPT is supported. Spending less doesn't necessarily require giving up a paid plan altogether.
AI subscriptions have another unusual wrinkle: the product can change while you are paying for it. OpenAI retired GPT-4o from ChatGPT on February 13, 2026, after previously restoring it when some Plus and Pro users said they preferred its conversational style. For someone who subscribed partly for access to a particular model, that's a reminder that a paid AI service can change substantially from one month to the next.
Features and price aren't the only reasons someone might reconsider a paid ChatGPT plan. After OpenAI's February 2026 agreement with the US Department of Defense to deploy its models on the department's classified network, Sensor Tower data reported by TechCrunch showed US ChatGPT app uninstalls jumping 295 percent day over day. OpenAI later amended the agreement to explicitly prohibit domestic surveillance of US persons and said its services would not be used by Defense Department intelligence agencies such as the NSA without a new agreement. The Sensor Tower figure measures app uninstalls, though, not paid subscription cancellations.
How to cancel your ChatGPT subscription
For a personal subscription purchased on chatgpt.com, log in, select your profile icon, open Settings, choose Billing and select Cancel under Cancel plan. OpenAI recommends canceling at least 24 hours before the next billing date to avoid another charge.
If you subscribed through Apple, open the iPhone Settings app, tap your name, tap Subscriptions, select ChatGPT and tap Cancel Subscription. On Android, open Google Play, make sure you're signed in with the Google account used for the purchase, then go to Subscriptions > ChatGPT and tap Cancel subscription. Uninstalling the app does not cancel an App Store or Google Play subscription.
If you can't find the cancel option, first check where you originally subscribed. Web, Apple and Google subscriptions are managed separately, and OpenAI warns that it's possible to end up with more than one active subscription across those platforms. If you have lost access to the ChatGPT account or its email address, OpenAI support can also cancel the subscription after locating the account using the email address, the last four digits of the payment card and the date of the most recent payment.
What canceling a ChatGPT subscription does and doesn't change
Canceling the subscription stops future renewals, but it doesn't delete your OpenAI account or erase existing chats. Standard chats remain saved to your account until you delete them, so canceling a paid plan is not the same thing as removing your data.
Whether your chats are used for model training is controlled separately. Under Settings > Data Controls, turning off Improve the model for everyone prevents new conversations from being used to improve OpenAI's models while leaving those conversations in your history. Temporary Chats are another option for individual conversations: they don't appear in history or get used to improve the models, and OpenAI says it may keep a copy for up to 30 days for safety purposes.
Deleting your OpenAI account is separate from canceling the subscription. Account deletion is permanent, prevents access to OpenAI services and triggers deletion of account data within 30 days, apart from limited information OpenAI may retain where required or permitted by law. If Apple or Google is billing you, cancel the subscription through the relevant app store before deleting the account.
What happens after you cancel ChatGPT
Canceling doesn't remove paid features immediately. OpenAI says the cancellation becomes effective the day after the next billing date, so you can keep using the paid plan through the current billing period.
Canceling also doesn't automatically result in a refund. If you subscribed through chatgpt.com or Google Play, you can request one through OpenAI's Help Center. App Store refunds must be requested directly from Apple. For chatgpt.com and Google Play purchases, accidental purchases are generally eligible for a refund if you contact OpenAI within 14 days of the charge.
Customers in the EU, UKand Turkey are also eligible for a prorated refund if they cancel within 14 days of purchase.
Once the paid period ends, your account remains available along with any chats you haven't deleted. Canceling the subscription stops the recurring payment without requiring you to decide whether to keep using ChatGPT.

AI subscriptions have another unusual wrinkle: the product can change while you are paying for it. OpenAI retired GPT-4o from ChatGPT on February 13, 2026, after previously restoring it when some Plus and Pro users said they preferred its conversational style. For someone who subscribed partly for access to a particular model, that's a reminder that a paid AI service can change substantially from one month to the next.
Features and price aren't the only reasons someone might reconsider a paid ChatGPT plan. After OpenAI's February 2026 agreement with the US Department of Defense to deploy its models on the department's classified network, Sensor Tower data reported by TechCrunch showed US ChatGPT app uninstalls jumping 295 percent day over day. OpenAI later amended the agreement to explicitly prohibit domestic surveillance of US persons and said its services would not be used by Defense Department intelligence agencies such as the NSA without a new agreement. The Sensor Tower figure measures app uninstalls, though, not paid subscription cancellations.
How to cancel your ChatGPT subscription
For a personal subscription purchased on chatgpt.com, log in, select your profile icon, open Settings, choose Billing and select Cancel under Cancel plan. OpenAI recommends canceling at least 24 hours before the next billing date to avoid another charge.
If you subscribed through Apple, open the iPhone Settings app, tap your name, tap Subscriptions, select ChatGPT and tap Cancel Subscription. On Android, open Google Play, make sure you're signed in with the Google account used for the purchase, then go to Subscriptions > ChatGPT and tap Cancel subscription. Uninstalling the app does not cancel an App Store or Google Play subscription.
If you can't find the cancel option, first check where you originally subscribed. Web, Apple and Google subscriptions are managed separately, and OpenAI warns that it's possible to end up with more than one active subscription across those platforms. If you have lost access to the ChatGPT account or its email address, OpenAI support can also cancel the subscription after locating the account using the email address, the last four digits of the payment card and the date of the most recent payment.
What canceling a ChatGPT subscription does and doesn't change
Canceling the subscription stops future renewals, but it doesn't delete your OpenAI account or erase existing chats. Standard chats remain saved to your account until you delete them, so canceling a paid plan is not the same thing as removing your data.
Whether your chats are used for model training is controlled separately. Under Settings > Data Controls, turning off Improve the model for everyone prevents new conversations from being used to improve OpenAI's models while leaving those conversations in your history. Temporary Chats are another option for individual conversations: they don't appear in history or get used to improve the models, and OpenAI says it may keep a copy for up to 30 days for safety purposes.
Deleting your OpenAI account is separate from canceling the subscription. Account deletion is permanent, prevents access to OpenAI services and triggers deletion of account data within 30 days, apart from limited information OpenAI may retain where required or permitted by law. If Apple or Google is billing you, cancel the subscription through the relevant app store before deleting the account.
What happens after you cancel ChatGPT
Canceling doesn't remove paid features immediately. OpenAI says the cancellation becomes effective the day after the next billing date, so you can keep using the paid plan through the current billing period.
Canceling also doesn't automatically result in a refund. If you subscribed through chatgpt.com or Google Play, you can request one through OpenAI's Help Center. App Store refunds must be requested directly from Apple. For chatgpt.com and Google Play purchases, accidental purchases are generally eligible for a refund if you contact OpenAI within 14 days of the charge.
Customers in the EU, UKand Turkey are also eligible for a prorated refund if they cancel within 14 days of purchase.
Once the paid period ends, your account remains available along with any chats you haven't deleted. Canceling the subscription stops the recurring payment without requiring you to decide whether to keep using ChatGPT.

title_en: Zillow and Redfin settle FTC antitrust case over their rental listings partnership
title_fa: Zillow and Redfin settle FTC antitrust case over their rental listings partnership
excerpt_en: The FTC and Zillow have announced a settlement that ends the case alleging that a 2025 "partnership" between Zillow and Redfin violated antitrust laws. The FTC had alleged Zillow agreed to pay Redfin to syndicate its listings, while Redfin would end its own advertising contracts...
excerpt_fa: The FTC and Zillow have announced a settlement that ends the case alleging that a 2025 "partnership" between Zillow and Redfin violated antitrust laws. The FTC had alleged Zillow agreed to pay Redfin to syndicate its listings, while Redfin would end its own advertising contracts...
content_en:
The FTC and Zillow have announced a settlement that ends the case alleging that a 2025 “partnership” between Zillow and Redfin violated antitrust laws. The FTC had alleged Zillow agreed to pay Redfin to syndicate its listings, while Redfin would end its own advertising contracts and promise not to compete with Zillow for multifamily listings.
Zillow and Redfin settle FTC antitrust case over their rental listings partnership
They had allegedly conspired to reduce competition in rental listings, leaving fewer options and higher prices.
They had allegedly conspired to reduce competition in rental listings, leaving fewer options and higher prices.
The FTC’s settlement proposal allows Redfin to continue syndicating rental listings from Zillow “unencumbered by the anticompetitive restraints” in the original deal, but also requires Redfin to restart its own rental listings advertising business, which it wound down as part of the partnership.
Daniel Guarnera, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Competition, said the deal “delivers better, quicker, more certain results for both renters and property management companies than we would have been able to achieve after prevailing at trial.” The state attorneys general of Arizona, Connecticut, New York, Virginia and Washington also agreed to the proposed settlement.
This ending also follows other recent settlements from the Trump administration in high-profile cases of companies behaving badly, like the Live Nation-Ticketmaster case, and its case against Realpage.
content_fa:
FTC و Zillow توافقنامه ای را اعلام کرده اند که به این ادعا پایان می دهد که "مشارکت" 2025 بین Zillow و Redfin قوانین ضد تراست را نقض کرده است. FTC ادعا کرده بود که Zillow موافقت کرده است که به Redfin برای سندیکا کردن فهرست‌هایش پول بدهد، در حالی که Redfin به قراردادهای تبلیغاتی خود پایان می‌دهد و قول می‌دهد که با Zillow برای فهرست‌های چند خانواده رقابت نکند.
Zillow و Redfin پرونده ضد انحصار FTC را در مورد شراکت خود در لیست اجاره حل و فصل می کنند
آنها ظاهراً برای کاهش رقابت در لیست اجاره‌ها توطئه کرده بودند و گزینه‌های کمتر و قیمت‌های بالاتری را باقی گذاشتند.
آنها ظاهراً برای کاهش رقابت در لیست اجاره‌ها توطئه کرده بودند و گزینه‌های کمتر و قیمت‌های بالاتری را باقی گذاشتند.
پیشنهاد تسویه حساب FTC به Redfin این امکان را می دهد که به اشتراک لیست های اجاره از Zillow "بدون محدودیت های ضدرقابتی" در قرارداد اصلی ادامه دهد، اما همچنین Redfin را ملزم می کند تا تجارت تبلیغات لیست اجاره خود را که به عنوان بخشی از شراکت منحل می شود، از سر بگیرد.
دانیل گوارنا، مدیر دفتر رقابت FTC، گفت که این معامله "نتایج بهتر، سریع‌تر و مطمئن‌تری را هم برای اجاره‌کنندگان و هم برای شرکت‌های مدیریت املاک نسبت به آنچه که پس از پیروزی در آزمایشی می‌توانستیم به دست آوریم، ارائه می‌دهد." دادستان های کل ایالت های آریزونا، کانکتیکات، نیویورک، ویرجینیا و واشنگتن نیز با توافق پیشنهادی موافقت کردند.
این پایان همچنین به دنبال تسویه حساب های اخیر دولت ترامپ در پرونده های پرمخاطب رفتار بد شرکت ها، مانند پرونده Live Nation-Ticketmaster و پرونده آن علیه Realpage است.

title_en: ESPN is raising prices on most of its streaming subscriptions, even bundles with Disney+
title_fa: ESPN is raising prices on most of its streaming subscriptions, even bundles with Disney+
excerpt_en: ESPN's Unlimited tier will cost $32 per month as of September 17.
excerpt_fa: ESPN's Unlimited tier will cost $32 per month as of September 17.
content_en:
ESPN is raising prices on most of its streaming subscriptions, even bundles with Disney+
The Unlimited tier will cost $32 per month as of September 17.
Do you hear the rustling in the wind? It's another streaming platform getting ready to raise prices. ESPN is increasing the cost of every single one of its subscription plans, according to reporting by Sports Media Watch. These price bumps take effect on September 17.
ESPN Unlimited, which provides access to the streaming platform and all affiliated live broadcast feeds, is shooting up to $32 a month from $30. The annual plan is going up to $320 from $300.
The Select tier includes many ad-supported live events, overflow content and access to original documentaries and studio shows, but no live feeds of the actual channels. That one's going up to $14 from $13. The annual plan will cost $140 instead of $130.
This is even impacting many bundles with Disney+. The combo subscription that includes ad-supported versions of Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Select will soon cost $22 per month instead of $20. The ad-free version is going up to $33 each month instead of $30. However, bundles that include ESPN Unlimited look to be safe from the increase fairy for now. This is likely because it was recently revealed that 80 percent of Unlimited subscribers are part of one of those Disney+/Hulu bundles.
This is the first price increase for the ESPN streaming platform. However, it just launched last year. Given the state of the industry, it could raise prices again this time next September. Many modern streamers, like Peacock and Netflix, have been forcing increases on an annual basis.

title_en: Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
title_fa: Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
excerpt_en: Robotaxis are expanding. So is the fight over the rules governing them. In New York, Gov. Kathy Hochul withdrew a proposal earlier this year that would have opened the door to driverless robotaxis outside New York City after taxi drivers, unions, and state lawmakers opposed it....
excerpt_fa: Robotaxis are expanding. So is the fight over the rules governing them. In New York, Gov. Kathy Hochul withdrew a proposal earlier this year that would have opened the door to driverless robotaxis outside New York City after taxi drivers, unions, and state lawmakers opposed it....
content_en:
Robotaxis are expanding. So is the fight over the rules governing them.
Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
As more robotaxis hit the road, the fight over the rules governing the technology is intensifying.
Robotaxis are real now — so is the pushback
As more robotaxis hit the road, the fight over the rules governing the technology is intensifying.
In New York, Gov. Kathy Hochul withdrew a proposal earlier this year that would have opened the door to driverless robotaxis outside New York City after taxi drivers, unions, and state lawmakers opposed it. Six months later, commercial driverless service remains illegal in the state, and legalization efforts are stalled.
In DC, labor unions are fighting legislation that would legalize commercial robotaxis, while lawmakers are weighing a 200-vehicle cap and a 15-cent-per-mile fee that would fund Metro upgrades and aid workers displaced by autonomous vehicles. A July City Council hearing on the proposal stretched for a grueling 10 hours.
In San Francisco, Mayor Daniel Lurie, a vocal supporter of robotaxis, is now calling for tougher robotaxi regulations after Waymos repeatedly snarled traffic during emergencies and major events. And as of July, California police can now formally cite autonomous-vehicle manufacturers when their driverless cars break traffic laws.
And while Congress has yet to pass comprehensive robotaxi legislation, federal regulators have stepped up their scrutiny. The Trump administration’s National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recently warned autonomous-vehicle companies that vehicles unable to safely interact with police, firefighters, and other first responders pose a danger to the public.
Even in states that have broadly welcomed autonomous vehicles, governments are grappling with how to oversee them. Texas this year began enforcing new permitting requirements for commercial AV operators, while cities in Florida have complained that state preemption laws leave them with little power to respond to problems on their own streets.
Even in states that have broadly welcomed autonomous vehicles, governments are grappling with how to oversee them
Taxi drivers, labor unions, and safety advocates have fought autonomous vehicles for years. What’s changing is the scale and immediacy of the fight. Now that robotaxis have burst free from the pages of science fiction and onto actual city streets, policymakers are confronting a messier reality filled with questions about safety, regulation, growth, and jobs. They’re having to decide how quickly fleets should be allowed to expand, what companies must prove before they do, and how much control cities and states should have over their operations.
Waymo, the market leader, is currently operating more than 3,500 vehicles publicly in 11 US cities. Zoox — a purpose-built robotaxi without a steering wheel that bears a striking resemblance to a toaster — just began offering paid rides in Las Vegas and continues to offer free trips to users of its Explorer program in San Francisco as it collects feedback. It’s testing in a total of 10 cities and plans to extend the Explorer program to Austin and Miami later this year. Tesla, which began its Robotaxi rollout with a safety monitor aboard more than a year ago, appears to finally be growing its unsupervised fleet ahead of launching its purpose-built robotaxi, the Cybercab, later this month.
Still, for all the political attention, robotaxis remain a tiny share of the US ridehailing market. While Waymo now provides more than 500,000 paid rides a week, Uber handles about 40 million trips a day globally. At that scale, robotaxis haven’t yet displaced many driving jobs or fundamentally changed how cities move. But their visibility vastly exceeds their market share, especially when a driverless car stops in the wrong place during a blackout or interferes with an emergency response.
And the consequences could look very different as autonomous fleets grow from thousands of vehicles to hundreds of thousands. That’s why the battles taking shape across the country are increasingly about the terms of expansion: what companies have to prove before they grow, what they owe cities and workers, and how much control cities and states should have over their operations.
What the critics want
In many places, the robotaxi rollout has outpaced the rules governing it.
“Robotaxis are popping up all over the place,” said Shua Sanchez, national campaign director of SAVE-US, a nonprofit advocating for stricter state AV legislation in the absence of federal rules. “The state legislatures don’t have experience with this technology, and there aren’t good laws on the books to regulate them.”
SAVE-US is working with lawmakers in New Jersey and New York on a three-pronged approach. It wants multi-stage testing and commercial-deployment permits, under which companies would have to demonstrate their vehicles can operate safely with a small fleet before adding more cars, while continuing to share safety data after commercial service begins. It also wants autonomous vehicles to use multiple kinds of sensors, rather than relying on cameras alone (as Tesla does), and is calling for restrictions on marketing terms like “Autopilot” or “Full Self-Driving” for consumer driver-assist features when the systems still require human oversight.
The group isn’t opposed to autonomous vehicles, Sanchez said, but is “pro the safe development of technology.” He added that AV safety isn’t a settled question, and that even a strong record today doesn’t guarantee the same after a software or hardware change.
Sen. Ed Markey (D-MA), who has pushed for greater federal oversight of AVs, makes a similar argument about transparency.
“Autonomous vehicle companies are making huge claims about how their technology is going to save lives,” Markey told The Verge in a statement. “But right now, our regulatory structure amounts to this: we hope they’re telling the truth.”

title_en: What are the downsides of a mini PC?
title_fa: What are the downsides of a mini PC?
excerpt_en: Small space means less cooling, which in turn means less sustained power.
excerpt_fa: فضای کوچک به معنای خنک کننده کمتر است که به نوبه خود به معنای قدرت پایدار کمتر است.
content_en:
What are the downsides of a mini PC?
Small space means less cooling, which in turn means less sustained power.
Mini PCs have become a popular alternative to full-size desktops and laptops over recent years. Brands like Geekom, Beelink and Minisforum have appeared, almost overnight, with machines that can fit in your hand while offering performance that can sometimes rival their bigger siblings.
The physical footprint of a mini PC is both a blessing and a curse. Mini PCs are designed to be full desktop replacements, but their size means that they can be tricky to upgrade and even harder to keep cool. Before you rush into mini PC ownership, you'll want to consider these downsides.
Limited options for upgrades
Mini PCs can range in price, from ultra-budget to serious AI workstations, but their components don't differ much from what you'd find in a laptop. Like a laptop, these machines aren't really designed to be upgraded. You aren't expected to be able to swap out a motherboard or replace the CPU. In fact, the CPU and GPU are often soldered onto the motherboard. Unless you're handy with a soldering iron, there's no real route forward to switch these out.
If your mini PC can be upgraded at all, it'll usually allow you to swap out the SSD or RAM. Mini PCs typically come with SO-DIMM memory modules, as well as smaller M.2 SSDs, both of which you'll also find in a modern laptop. It isn't always a given that these are components you can replace, though. You'll find mini PCs on sale that feature both soldered memory and storage that prevent any possibility of future upgrades.
By design, you've also got few options for expansion. The limited space inside a mini PC case means it's unlikely that you'll find extra RAM or SSD slots for upgrades. External I/O might be limited, too, with a smaller number of USB ports, for example.
Some mid-tier and better mini PCs come with OCuLink or Thunderbolt USB-C ports that allow you to connect an external GPU inside an enclosure. This won't allow you to upgrade your mini PC directly, but it can give you extra power for gaming or workstation AI requirements, with some loss of performance compared to a desktop PC.
You've also got a longevity issue. Cheap mini PCs aren't running with the most powerful components, so once they're too slow to use effectively, replacing it fully could be your only option.
Cooling and performance can't compare to a desktop PC
For mini PC owners, performance is a matter of compromise and sacrifice. By choosing the smallest form factor, mini PC owners are choosing to own a machine with none of the air-cooling benefits of a bigger desktop. Space is the limiting factor, as sizing down means there's much less space for fans to be able to circulate cooler air in and out. While mini PCs are designed with complex cooling systems to try and offset this, they can only go so far: you're not achieving RTX 5090-level gaming prowess with one.
That's not to say that powerful mini PCs don't exist, powered by CPUs like the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, which offer performance power to rival desktop equivalent CPUs like the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X. These machines may be closing the gap to rival larger desktops for their CPU performance, but the physical limitations remain. It all comes back to raw power. Sustained performance under heavy load means more heat, and more cooling. Mini PCs are at a disadvantage here compared to desktop PCs, which have more fans or liquid cooling to push components harder.
Laptops offer a similar challenge from a build perspective, with cooling and power that's tricky to scale upwards. Like high-end laptops, mini PCs that can deliver high-end performance will get very hot and, as a result, will become very noisy under sustained loads. There's no way around this. Being built inside a mini PC case means it's an even harder job for the machine to stay cool enough to keep running. Traditional liquid cooling isn't a practical option due to the limited space, either.
Admittedly, this isn't as big an issue with low-power mini PCs. The modern, low-end CPUs used in laptops and mini PCs are typically more power efficient, generating less heat simply by using less electrical power. The compromise here, however, is that performance won't compare to a high-end machine.
Mini PCs aren't designed to be user repairable
Building a desktop PC, even inside a smaller case, will leave you with some options for repairability. If the power supply blows up, assuming no other components are damaged, you can swap it out. If the components are damaged, you can replace them, too.
With a mini PC, you don't have the same luxury, as they aren't designed to be repairable in the same way as a desktop PC. Instead, you can treat a mini PC like you would a laptop. Should the CPU or motherboard fail, sourcing a replacement from a retailer will not be an option. Instead, you'll be left to look at your options for repair under warranty or, more likely, just buying a new one.
Mini PCs can be a poor value investment
The Beelink SER5. The Asus ROG NUC 16. These products exist at both extreme ends of the PC hardware market, with the former priced at $389, and the latter priced as high as $4,999. Yet, they're both mini PCs. They fit inside small (or reasonably small) cases, feature mobile-grade components and use less electrical power than a desktop PC.
To match a desktop PC's raw power, or even get close, you'll be paying a premium. $5,000 will still get you an extremely powerful traditional desktop PC with better performance and more room for future upgrades compared to mini PCs like the NUC 16. That's even more important as we see prices going up across the board, thanks to the spiralling costs for RAM and SSDs caused by AI.
This makes the value of investing in a mini PC harder to justify. If you have $5,000 to spend on an Asus ROG NUC 15, or even just $400 to spend on the Beelink SER5, you could choose to buy a laptop or PC from a better-known brand to last you five years or...

This won't allow you to upgrade your mini PC directly, but it can give you extra power for gaming or workstation AI requirements, with some loss of performance compared to a desktop PC.
You've also got a longevity issue. Cheap mini PCs aren't running with the most powerful components, so once they're too slow to use effectively, replacing it fully could be your only option.
Cooling and performance can't compare to a desktop PC
For mini PC owners, performance is a matter of compromise and sacrifice. By choosing the smallest form factor, mini PC owners are choosing to own a machine with none of the air-cooling benefits of a bigger desktop. Space is the limiting factor, as sizing down means there's much less space for fans to be able to circulate cooler air in and out. While mini PCs are designed with complex cooling systems to try and offset this, they can only go so far: you're not achieving RTX 5090-level gaming prowess with one.
That's not to say that powerful mini PCs don't exist, powered by CPUs like the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, which offer performance power to rival desktop equivalent CPUs like the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X. These machines may be closing the gap to rival larger desktops for their CPU performance, but the physical limitations remain. It all comes back to raw power. Sustained performance under heavy load means more heat, and more cooling. Mini PCs are at a disadvantage here compared to desktop PCs, which have more fans or liquid cooling to push components harder.
Laptops offer a similar challenge from a build perspective, with cooling and power that's tricky to scale upwards. Like high-end laptops, mini PCs that can deliver high-end performance will get very hot and, as a result, will become very noisy under sustained loads. There's no way around this. Being built inside a mini PC case means it's an even harder job for the machine to stay cool enough to keep running. Traditional liquid cooling isn't a practical option due to the limited space, either.
Admittedly, this isn't as big an issue with low-power mini PCs. The modern, low-end CPUs used in laptops and mini PCs are typically more power efficient, generating less heat simply by using less electrical power. The compromise here, however, is that performance won't compare to a high-end machine.
Mini PCs aren't designed to be user repairable
Building a desktop PC, even inside a smaller case, will leave you with some options for repairability. If the power supply blows up, assuming no other components are damaged, you can swap it out. If the components are damaged, you can replace them, too.
With a mini PC, you don't have the same luxury, as they aren't designed to be repairable in the same way as a desktop PC. Instead, you can treat a mini PC like you would a laptop. Should the CPU or motherboard fail, sourcing a replacement from a retailer will not be an option. Instead, you'll be left to look at your options for repair under warranty or, more likely, just buying a new one.
Mini PCs can be a poor value investment
The Beelink SER5. The Asus ROG NUC 16. These products exist at both extreme ends of the PC hardware market, with the former priced at $389, and the latter priced as high as $4,999. Yet, they're both mini PCs. They fit inside small (or reasonably small) cases, feature mobile-grade components and use less electrical power than a desktop PC.
To match a desktop PC's raw power, or even get close, you'll be paying a premium. $5,000 will still get you an extremely powerful traditional desktop PC with better performance and more room for future upgrades compared to mini PCs like the NUC 16. That's even more important as we see prices going up across the board, thanks to the spiralling costs for RAM and SSDs caused by AI.
This makes the value of investing in a mini PC harder to justify. If you have $5,000 to spend on an Asus ROG NUC 15, or even just $400 to spend on the Beelink SER5, you could choose to buy a laptop or PC from a better-known brand to last you five years or...

CD Projekt Red is aiming to launch The Witcher 4 sometime in 2028, joint CEO Michał Nowakowski says in a new video.
