The Witcher 4 developers target a 2028 release
CD Projekt Red’s big Witcher sequel is still a couple years away.
CD Projekt Red’s big Witcher sequel is still a couple years away.
There’s more new Witcher to come before The Witcher 4, though. At this week’s Gamescom event, CD Projekt Red will be showing off its upcoming Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, which is scheduled to release sometime in 2027. Songs of the Past is also set to be part of Gamescom’s Opening Night Live event hosted by Geoff Keighley, which kicks off at 2PM ET on Tuesday.
CD Projekt Red is also working on a multiplayer spinoff set in the universe of The Witcher that’s codenamed Project Siris. Earlier in August, the company confirmed that it laid off staff working on the game.

title_en: Zillow settles antitrust lawsuit with the FTC
title_fa: Zillow settles antitrust lawsuit with the FTC
excerpt_en: Zillow settles antitrust lawsuit with the FTC.
excerpt_fa: Zillow settles antitrust lawsuit with the FTC.
content_en:
Zillow settles antitrust lawsuit with the FTC
Competitor Redfin will re-enter the real estate listing market.
After accusations of Zillow buying off its rival Redfin for $100 million, the online real estate platform has settled an antitrust lawsuit brought on by the Federal Trade Commission. According to a press release from the FTC, the two sides resolved the lawsuit and reversed an agreement from Zillow that shut down Redfin's internet listing service (ILS) for apartment rentals.
As part of the settlement, Redfin has to reenter the ILS market and make commitments that would ensure its competitiveness, including a relaunch with "significantly more listings," according to the FTC. The FTC said that "restoring competition in the ILS market is expected to drive down costs and spur innovation that benefits renters and property management companies."
The lawsuit was first filed in September 2025 when the FTC accused Zillow of buying out a rival company by offering $100 million to Redfin to halt its ILS advertising for up to nine years. Arizona, Connecticut, New York, Virginia and Washington also jointly filed a similar lawsuit against Zillow, which was eventually merged with the FTC's suit in November of that year.
Beyond Redfin restarting its efforts to market apartment listings, the settlement requires Zillow to provide Redfin with employee information to allow for employee recruitment. On the consumer side, Zillow has to offer its customers the ability to renegotiate their contracts without any extra cost or penalty as part of the settlement.
content_fa:
Zillow دعوای ضد تراست را با FTC حل و فصل می کند
رقیب Redfin دوباره وارد بازار فهرست املاک و مستغلات خواهد شد.
پس از اتهامات وارده به Zillow مبنی بر خرید رقیب خود Redfin به قیمت 100 میلیون دلار، پلتفرم آنلاین املاک و مستغلات یک شکایت ضد تراست که توسط کمیسیون تجارت فدرال مطرح شده بود را حل و فصل کرد. بر اساس بیانیه مطبوعاتی FTC، دو طرف این دعوا را حل و فصل کردند و توافقنامه Zillow را لغو کردند که خدمات لیست اینترنتی Redfin (ILS) را برای اجاره آپارتمان تعطیل می کرد.
به‌عنوان بخشی از توافق، Redfin باید دوباره وارد بازار ILS شود و تعهداتی را بپذیرد که رقابت‌پذیری آن را تضمین می‌کند، از جمله راه‌اندازی مجدد با «فهرست‌های بسیار بیشتر»، طبق گفته FTC. FTC گفت که "انتظار می رود بازگرداندن رقابت در بازار ILS باعث کاهش هزینه ها و تحریک نوآوری شود که به نفع اجاره دهندگان و شرکت های مدیریت املاک است."
این شکایت اولین بار در سپتامبر 2025 زمانی که FTC Zillow را به خرید یک شرکت رقیب با پیشنهاد 100 میلیون دلاری به Redfin برای توقف تبلیغات ILS خود تا 9 سال متهم کرد. آریزونا، کانکتیکات، نیویورک، ویرجینیا و واشنگتن نیز به طور مشترک شکایت مشابهی را علیه Zillow تنظیم کردند که در نهایت با شکایت FTC در نوامبر همان سال ادغام شد.
فراتر از شروع مجدد تلاش های Redfin برای بازاریابی لیست آپارتمان ها، تسویه حساب از Zillow می خواهد که اطلاعات کارمندان را به Redfin ارائه دهد تا امکان استخدام کارمندان را فراهم کند. در سمت مصرف کننده، Zillow باید به مشتریان خود این امکان را ارائه دهد که در قراردادهای خود بدون هیچ هزینه یا جریمه اضافی به عنوان بخشی از تسویه حساب، مذاکره کنند.

title_en: Hot vs cold: What's the ideal temperature for solar panel efficiency?
title_fa: Hot vs cold: What's the ideal temperature for solar panel efficiency?
excerpt_en: Will solar panels work well in your location? Solar panel efficiency depends on several factors, including temperature.
excerpt_fa: Will solar panels work well in your location? Solar panel efficiency depends on several factors, including temperature.
content_en:
Hot vs cold: What's the ideal temperature for solar panel efficiency?
There is a correct answer, but ambient temperature is just one of several variables.
Sunlight is a solar panel's best friend. But heat, not so much.
The most common number you will see is 77 degrees Fahrenheit. That is 25 degrees Celsius, which is the temperature of the cell when manufacturers rate panels under standard test conditions, alongside irradiance of 1,000 watts per square meter. It's a good indicator, but it's not a magic outdoor temperature at which your roof achieves peak output.
So yeah, cold wins, technically. The efficiency of solar cells is typically higher at lower temperatures because the voltage decreases more than the current increases with temperature. The problem is that efficiency and total electricity production are not the same. A cold panel might generate more power from the same amount of sunlight, but a hot summer day might generate more power because there might be more sunlight.
Why solar panels lose efficiency as they get hotter
The first wrinkle is that the temperature on your weather app isn't necessarily the temperature of the panel. A module in direct sunlight can be much hotter than the ambient air temperature, and Sandia National Laboratories, a US Department of Energy lab, models module temperature based on ambient temperature, solar irradiance, wind speed and mounting configuration.
As soon as the cells get hotter than their rated reference temperature, output begins to drop according to the panel's temperature coefficient. There isn't one universal 0.5 percent penalty. REC Group, a leading solar panel manufacturer, has a maximum-power temperature coefficient of -0.24 percent per degree Celsius for its current Alpha Pure-RX, while solar manufacturer Qcells lists -0.29 percent per degree Celsius for its residential Q.TRON BLK M-G2+ series. If you live in a place that's really hot, that's something to consider.
Nor is 77 degrees Fahrenheit "too hot" in the sense that the panel is in danger. The Q.TRON model has a continuous operating range of up to 158 degrees Fahrenheit, according to Qcells. REC lists a T98 module operating temperature of 176 degrees Fahrenheit for the Alpha Pure-RX. The Department of Energy says extreme heat can still damage cells and other module materials and shorten their operating lifetimes.
The best weather for efficiency isn't always the best for production
This is where the simple hot vs cold answer gets complicated. While a bright, cold day can be great for solar efficiency, clouds, snow, roof orientation, sun angle and daylight hours may be more important to the amount of electricity your system can generate.
So the best time is not necessarily 10AM to 4PM. Output generally rises as more direct sunlight reaches the panels, then falls later in the day, but an east-facing array will be different from a west-facing array. Although panels can run hotter in the summer, the longer days and often stronger solar resources can result in more total electricity being produced.
That's also why some homeowners size a solar system above their typical electricity needs. The 20 percent rule for solar panels is based on giving a solar system some breathing room when conditions aren't ideal.
The National Laboratory of the Rockies' PVWatts calculator (the lab's free online estimator) allows you to input location and system information to estimate monthly and annual production, which gives you a more specific answer than "summer" or "midday." NLR does not specify a single best month or time of day, and it cautions that PVWatts cannot account for all site-specific variations or differentiate between higher- and lower-performing PV technologies.
Its expected production range is based on 30 years of actual weather data.

title_en: Valor, Point72 back General Intuition at $6B valuation as AI startup pushes into robotics
title_fa: Valor، Point72 از General Intuition با ارزش 6 میلیارد دلار حمایت می کند زیرا استارتاپ هوش مصنوعی به سمت روباتیک پیش می رود.
excerpt_en: General Intuition, the startup building a foundation model that trains generalized AI agents how to move through space and time, is in talks to raise at a $6 billion pre-money valuation from new investors including Valor Ventures, Point72 Ventures, and Seven Seven Six.
excerpt_fa: General Intuition، استارت‌آپی که یک مدل پایه ایجاد می‌کند که به عوامل هوش مصنوعی تعمیم‌یافته نحوه حرکت در فضا و زمان را آموزش می‌دهد، در حال مذاکره برای افزایش ارزش ۶ میلیارد دلاری پیش از پول از سرمایه‌گذاران جدید از جمله Valor Ventures، Point72 Ventures و Seven Seven Six است.
content_en:
New York-based General Intuition, the startup building a foundation model that trains generalized AI agents to move through space and time, is in talks to raise funding at a $6 billion pre-money valuation from new investors including Valor Equity Partners, Point72 Ventures, and Seven Seven Six, according to sources familiar with the matter.
Existing investors including Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst are also participating in the round. The fresh funds would come just weeks after General Intuition raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation.
The news confirms earlier reporting on the deal for what is becoming one of the hottest startups tackling physical AI.
CEO Pim de Witte spun out General Intuition last October from his video game clip-sharing platform Medal, using its hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay and “action labels” — records of which buttons a player pressed and when — as an initial dataset.
Investor Vinod Khosla recently told TechCrunch that he believes those action labels will be a key part of the “emergence of intuition,” or the ability for a model to truly generalize across tasks that it wasn’t explicitly trained on.
General Intuition is still finalizing the round, and a source close to the deal said that it is oversubscribed as the startup continues to field interest from investors. The company intends to use the funds to focus to improve its general model with a focus on robotic embodiments. That means spending more on compute infrastructure (the company has a partnership with neolab CoreWeave) and hiring more talent.
Valor Equity Partners is known for backing SpaceX. TechCrunch has reached out to confirm its investment in General Intuition, which would be the first AI lab the fund has invested in since SpaceX.
This story is developing. Please check back in for updates.

excerpt_fa: ESPN is hiking the price of its subscription on September 17th, a change that will also impact its bundles with Disney Plus. In a support page spotted earlier by Sports Media Watch, ESPN says its ad-supported Select membership will cost $13.99 instead of $12.99 / month, while...
content_en:
ESPN is hiking the price of its subscription on September 17th, a change that will also impact its bundles with Disney Plus. In a support page spotted earlier by Sports Media Watch, ESPN says its ad-supported Select membership will cost $13.99 instead of $12.99 / month, while its Unlimited plan will rise to $31.99 from $29.99 / month.
ESPN streaming plans are getting more expensive
Starting September 17th, a subscription to ESPN Unlimited will cost $31.99 per month.
Starting September 17th, a subscription to ESPN Unlimited will cost $31.99 per month.
The annual ESPN Select plan is also going to $139.99 from $129.99 / year, and the annual Unlimited tier is increasing to $319.99 from $299.99 / year. Meanwhile, Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Select are going up in price as well. Here’s a rundown of the changes:
- Disney Plus (with ads), Hulu (with ads), and ESPN Select: $21.99 / month, up from $19.99 / month.
- Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), ESPN Select: $32.99 / month, up from $29.99.
- Legacy Disney Plus (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free), and ESPN Select: $27.99 / month, up from $24.99 / month.
Disney Plus bundles with ESPN Unlimited aren’t affected. Last week, Axios reported that about 80 percent of Unlimited subscribers signed up through the bundle with Disney Plus and Hulu.
Though Disney last raised prices across its bundles last year, this is the first increase for ESPN, which rolled out its standalone streaming subscription last August. As part of the launch, ESPN updated its mobile app with a TikTok-like feed of videos and a personalized version of SportsCenter. ESPN also launched multiview in its app on major smart TV platforms.

title_en: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything. Will everyone use them?
title_fa: OpenAI در حال ساخت عوامل هوش مصنوعی برای همه چیز است. آیا همه از آنها استفاده خواهند کرد؟
excerpt_en: Inside the frontier lab’s push to bring AI agents from software engineers to the masses.
excerpt_fa: تلاش آزمایشگاه مرزی برای آوردن عوامل هوش مصنوعی از مهندسان نرم افزار به توده ها.
content_en:
How much control are you willing to give an LLM over your digital life?
Getting the most value from a model means giving it the keys. For a control freak or the AI-hesitant, it seems like a lot. For Andrew Ambrosino, the lead engineer for OpenAI’s desktop app, it’s the only way to test the future, which is why that app now has access to, and control over, his inbox, his Slack account, his phone, apps like Notion and Figma, and more.
“If I’m asking it to write a document, is there a possibility that it’s going to pull from a private DM on that subject and not know that it’s not supposed to share some info? Yes,” Ambrosino told TechCrunch. “I’ll do it for the job. I will take the personal hit here and there if I have to. And I haven’t had to.”
Ambrosino works on OpenAI’s biggest bet, ChatGPT Work, which was released last month and is available on the company’s lowest subscription tier, for $20 a month. The product is intended to allow white-collar workers to field AI agents — hooking LLMs up to the digital workflows used by accountants, investors, doctors, and everyone else whose day-to-day is dominated by their computer.
OpenAI’s marketing copy puts the goal succinctly: A world where “where [artificial] intelligence goes beyond answering questions to helping everyone turn their biggest ideas into reality.”
For software developers, that shift is already happening, but it’s been slow to spread to other departments. ChatGPT Work is a modified version of the company’s Codex coding tool. It’s meant to give non-engineers a version of the same functionality that software engineers already get from agents: an AI tool that doesn’t just answer questions, but completes multistep projects on its own.
“In this new factor, ChatGPT can actually do entire, very complicated tasks for you all autonomously in a way that is delightful and safe,” Thibault Sottiaux, who leads OpenAI’s core product work, including Work, told TechCrunch. “It’s the very mission of OpenAI — to bring everyone along.”
Commercially, that matters a lot. Agents that work for longer stretches burn through more tokens, which makes them more lucrative for OpenAI on a per-user basis. Reaching new professions is crucial — not just for OpenAI, but for the industry at large. If coding has proven lucrative territory for AI labs, it’s still a tiny subset of the professional work AI tools need to enable if these companies are to justify their massive investment in training and computation. While labs have been focused on software engineers, vertical-specific competitors like Harvey (for law) and Clay (for sales) have been chasing those customers with a model-agnostic approach, meaning they’ll plug in whichever AI works best at the time.
Industry analysts see this as one of the major challenges facing OpenAI and its competitors. “If the labs cannot rapidly get ahold of the key complementary assets needed to scale AI in the market, value will accrue elsewhere,” Christian Catalini wrote on a16z’s “It’s time to build” blog.
Making the AI apps work for people who aren’t software engineers requires more hand-holding. excerpt_fa: Raspberry Pi's head of social, Ashley Whittaker, acknowledged the cyberdeck trend today, saying "we haven't been able to get away from cyberdecks this year." Tiny portable computers made out of things like purses, jewelry boxes, and other thrifted or recycled parts have gone...
content_en:
Raspberry Pi’s head of social, Ashley Whittaker, acknowledged the cyberdeck trend today, saying “we haven’t been able to get away from cyberdecks this year.” Tiny portable computers made out of things like purses, jewelry boxes, and other thrifted or recycled parts have gone viral on TikTok and other social media platforms over the past year, and Raspberry Pi now has its own guide to building one of the homemade computers.
Raspberry Pi shares its official tutorial for making a cyberdeck
Homemade mini computers have been going viral lately, and this guide could give the trend a boost.
Homemade mini computers have been going viral lately, and this guide could give the trend a boost.
Raspberry Pi has also increased its prices multiple times this year due to rising costs for RAM and other components, which could be another reason to support this growing market of active and would-be hobbyists. The 16GB version of the Raspberry Pi 5 included in the company’s official cyberdeck guide got a $100 price hike in April, nearly as much as the board’s original $120 price.
Raspberry Pi’s cyberdeck guide includes a parts list and detailed assembly instructions, but sticks to a fairly simple design using a plain black Pelican-style case. As content creators are proving, though, you can make a cyberdeck out of just about anything. Annike Tan, whose cyberdecks have attracted millions of views on TikTok, continues to upgrade her “mermaid” purse cyberdeck with new design details and even added a USB hub.

title_en: Why are more movies not shot in IMAX?
title_fa: Why are more movies not shot in IMAX?
excerpt_en: Shooting an IMAX movie is an expensive endeavor that most filmmakers avoid, at least for now.
excerpt_fa: Shooting an IMAX movie is an expensive endeavor that most filmmakers avoid, at least for now.
content_en:
Why are more movies not shot in IMAX?
Shooting an IMAX movie is an expensive endeavor that most filmmakers avoid, at least for now.
IMAX movies are dramatic experiences: big, bold, bright, with a sense of scale that's much bigger than the average cinema screen. It's a demanding process for filmmakers to create IMAX movies, requiring specialist equipment and a big budget.
Only a select few, like Christopher Nolan, have fully embraced the standard, with Nolan's latest movie, The Odyssey, being one of the few to be filmed entirely on IMAX film. IMAX films deliver the goods — but if the format is so impressive, why aren't more movies being shot in IMAX?
IMAX film has always been difficult to shoot
IMAX isn't a new development, but it wasn't designed with Hollywood cinema in mind. The first IMAX film, Tiger Child, was a Japanese short film released in 1970, with a later film, North of Superior, used in 1971 to more widely showcase the format. Its early years were dominated by documentaries, educational films and more short films to showcase IMAX's huge screen size and high-resolution detail.
It's not a platform that has ever seen a huge amount of adoption. Shooting an IMAX film has always required bigger and more cumbersome equipment. Modern IMAX film cameras are still larger and heavier than their traditional counterparts, and are louder to operate, adding extra difficulty on a film set where clean audio is a necessity. Their size and general bulkiness make them an impractical option for a lot of scenes. You're not taking an IMAX camera with you if you're filming on a small set, or if you need to film fast-paced action scenes, for example.
IMAX film itself is big and bulky, too. The 65-70mm size is much larger than traditional 35mm film, which gives it its impressive quality, but the camera physically can't hold as much. That means regular film changes, a problem faced by Tom Holland on The Odyssey film set, who mistook the regular three-minute stoppages for film changes as a critique on his performance. Given the filming schedule for a Hollywood movie, extra stoppages like this simply add to the cost.
So, to film in IMAX, you'll need specialist cameras that are bulky and harder to film with, require expensive film, and can lead to a longer film schedule. Even newer IMAX cameras, like the quieter 65mm IMAX Keighley camera used in The Odyssey, are still bulky to operate, weighing almost 400 pounds. Most movie theaters can't show true IMAX screens in the original 15/70 format, so the true experience is reserved to a much smaller set of cinema screens. Some digital cameras are now IMAX-certified, but these don't deliver the same quality as traditional 15/70 IMAX film.
As a result, most filmmakers have chosen to use IMAX selectively. The Dark Knight, another Christopher Nolan movie, was the first major Hollywood film to use IMAX for some of its scenes, reserving it for parts of the film that he believed its impressive detail would have the biggest impact. Nolan, however, is a rarity. Most producers aren't willing to accept the trade-offs and additional costs, while others more typically go down the IMAX-certified digital route instead.
Digital cinema made shooting movies easier and cheaper
If we count Nolan as one of IMAX's biggest cheerleaders, his decision to partially film The Dark Knight using IMAX cameras in 2008 is an interesting contrast to how filmmaking was shifting in this period away from traditional film. Hollywood wasn't going for bigger IMAX films, but instead moving to digital production.
It's not hard to see why. Traditional filmmaking requires physical film, larger cameras, longer takes and more extensive post-production to edit and cut down. You eliminate almost all of these stress points with digital film cameras: quieter, smaller, easier to handle. If you compare and contrast to IMAX, which we've already mentioned as being even bigger and louder than traditional 35mm film cameras, then IMAX already felt antiquated in 2008, let alone in 2026 for most directors.
Digital film production became the obvious and practical choice for Hollywood very quickly. Slumdog Millionaire, released a year after Nolan's Dark Knight in 2009, won the Oscar for Best Cinematography in the same year, the first digitally-shot movie to do so. The industry hasn't looked back. That left IMAX as an experimental and niche option for most filmmakers. Nolan, a traditionalist who uses physical 65mm IMAX film cameras, is an enthusiast for the format that few else are, believing that IMAX film offers the highest quality of any film format available today.
"Filmed for IMAX" movies are the alternative. Tom Cruise is one of the most recognizable names making movies like this, with Mission Impossible: The Final Reckoning filmed using Sony IMAX-certified digital cameras. They're designed to capture a bigger image area to fill IMAX's expanded 1.90:1 size, with quality good enough to create movies that can still take advantage of IMAX cinema screens.
Unlike Nolan's movies, however, The Final Reckoning isn't true IMAX. It can't scale to the full IMAX screen, with an aspect ratio smaller in size. Other movies, like Ant-Man and the Wasp, only manage to hit 1.90:1 for a portion of each film: at least 45 minutes is the aim for it to be given the 'Filmed for IMAX' tag. You also have 'Experience in IMAX' movies which are remastered from their original widescreen format to fill the bigger size but lacking the same IMAX quality.
IMAX is too niche and difficult to justify for most productions
A movie, filmed truly for IMAX cinema screens, is visually impressive, but out of reach for most filmmakers. You can consider all of the impracticalities, but cost trumps them all.
IMAX is a very expensive format to film on. It requires specialist cameras, film and operators trained to use it. Filming with it takes longer, and post-production longer still. Once it's filmed, it can only be experienced in its true format in just 41 movie...

title_en: Brake problems in GM EVs draw greater federal scrutiny
title_fa: مشکلات ترمز در خودروهای الکتریکی جنرال موتورز بررسی فدرال بیشتری را به دنبال دارد
excerpt_en: In one crash, the driver of a 2024 Blazer EV said they had to "deliberately steer the vehicle into a concrete curb" to slow it down and avoid a "catastrophic intersection collision."
excerpt_fa: در یکی از تصادفات، راننده یک بلیزر EV مدل 2024 گفت که برای کاهش سرعت آن و جلوگیری از «برخورد فاجعه بار در تقاطع» باید «عمداً وسیله نقلیه را به یک حاشیه سیمانی هدایت کنند».
content_en:
General Motors electric vehicles, including ones built in partnership with Honda, are now facing increased scrutiny from the top U.S. auto safety regulator after hundreds of incidents, more than 20 crashes or fires, and at least six injuries.
The brake problems also extend to some non-EV models, including the Chevy Colorado, GMC Canyon, and the Buick Enclave and Envision. More than 1 million vehicles may be affected.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) started its investigation in April 2024 after reports of trouble from owners of 2023 model year Cadillac Lyriq vehicles. The agency’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) said Monday that it was upgrading this probe to what’s known as an “engineering analysis.” That’s the highest level of investigation that ODI performs, and is often a step the office takes before telling a company to issue a recall.
The initial complaints ODI received two years ago typically involved owners describing receiving a “Brake System Failure” message when starting up the vehicle, or after coming to a complete stop. GM performed “several internal investigations” into the issue, according to ODI, and determined that the problem was linked to fractures in the spindle of its “eBoost” brake-by-wire system.
But ODI said on Monday that it kept receiving reports of a loss of braking assistance that were “inconsistent with GM’s description of a spindle failure.” The additional reports described an “immediate loss of brake assist” while a customer was in the process of braking to slow their car down, which the safety regulator said “could result in extended braking distance, which increases the risk of a crash or injury.” ODI said it needs to do a further analysis of the potential for failures in the eBoost system.
“The safety of our customers is the highest priority for the entire GM team,” the automaker said in a statement. “We take these reports seriously and have conducted a thorough investigation, determining the alleged condition does not present an unreasonable risk to motor vehicle safety. We will continue to cooperate with NHTSA as its investigation proceeds.”
The eBoost system was introduced in 2019 and gradually rolled out to more models over the years. The system ditches a traditional mechanical link between the brake pedal and the braking system, opting for an electronic one instead. This allows GM to change the brake “feel” in different driving modes. The automaker put eBoost on its most popular EVs, like the Blazer EV, Equinox EV, Cadillac Lyriq, and the Honda Prologue and Acura ZDX, which it made with Honda in a joint venture. The Cruise Origin — the purpose-built electric autonomous vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals, which GM abandoned in 2024 — also used eBoost.
In one crash reported to NHTSA, the driver of a 2025 Lyriq said they lost their brakes while trying to pull into a parking space in front of the store. The vehicle drove over the curb and crashed through the store front, coming to rest “mid-way in the store, amidst the furniture and store structure,” according to the driver.
In another, the driver of a 2024 Blazer EV said they had to “deliberately steer the vehicle into a concrete curb” to slow it down and avoid a “catastrophic intersection collision.”
This story has been updated with a statement from GM.
content_fa:
خودروهای برقی جنرال موتورز، از جمله خودروهایی که با مشارکت هوندا ساخته شده‌اند، اکنون پس از صدها حادثه، بیش از 20 تصادف یا آتش‌سوزی و حداقل 6 جراحت، با نظارت بیشتر از سوی بالاترین تنظیم کننده ایمنی خودرو ایالات متحده مواجه هستند.
مشکلات ترمز به برخی از مدل‌های غیر EV از جمله Chevy Colorado، GMC Canyon و Buick Enclave و Envision نیز کشیده شده است. ممکن است بیش از 1 میلیون وسیله نقلیه تحت تأثیر قرار گیرند.
اداره ملی ایمنی ترافیک بزرگراه (NHTSA) تحقیقات خود را در آوریل 2024 پس از گزارش هایی مبنی بر مشکل از سوی صاحبان خودروهای کادیلاک لیریک مدل 2023 آغاز کرد. دفتر تحقیقات نقص آژانس (ODI) روز دوشنبه گفت که این کاوشگر را به آنچه به عنوان "تحلیل مهندسی" شناخته می شود، ارتقا می دهد. این بالاترین سطح تحقیقاتی است که ODI انجام می‌دهد و اغلب گامی است که دفتر قبل از اینکه به شرکت بگوید فراخوانی صادر کند انجام می‌دهد.
شکایات اولیه ODI که دو سال پیش دریافت کرد، معمولاً شامل دریافت پیام «شکست سیستم ترمز» هنگام راه‌اندازی خودرو یا پس از توقف کامل بود. به گفته ODI، جنرال موتورز "چندین بررسی داخلی" را در مورد این موضوع انجام داد و تشخیص داد که این مشکل به شکستگی در دوک نخ ریسی سیستم ترمز با سیم "eBoost" خود مرتبط است.
اما ODI روز دوشنبه گفت که مدام گزارش‌هایی مبنی بر از دست دادن کمک ترمز دریافت می‌کند که «با توضیحات جنرال موتورز در مورد خرابی اسپیندل مغایرت دارد». گزارش‌های اضافی «از دست دادن فوری کمک ترمز» را در زمانی که مشتری در حال ترمزگیری برای کاهش سرعت خودرو خود بود، توصیف می‌کند، که تنظیم‌کننده ایمنی گفت: «می‌تواند منجر به افزایش فاصله ترمز شود که خطر تصادف یا جراحت را افزایش می‌دهد». ODI گفت که باید تجزیه و تحلیل بیشتری از احتمال خرابی در سیستم eBoost انجام دهد.
این خودروساز در بیانیه ای گفت: "ایمنی مشتریان ما بالاترین اولویت برای کل تیم جنرال موتورز است." ما این گزارش‌ها را جدی می‌گیریم و تحقیقات کاملی را انجام داده‌ایم، تشخیص اینکه شرایط ادعا شده خطر غیرمنطقی برای ایمنی وسایل نقلیه موتوری ایجاد نمی‌کند. ما به همکاری با NHTSA در ادامه تحقیقات ادامه خواهیم داد.
سیستم eBoost در سال 2019 معرفی شد و به تدریج در طول سال ها به مدل های بیشتری عرضه شد. این سیستم یک پیوند مکانیکی سنتی بین پدال ترمز و سیستم ترمز را قطع می کند و به جای آن یک الکترونیکی را انتخاب می کند. این به جنرال موتورز اجازه می‌دهد تا حس ترمز را در حالت‌های مختلف رانندگی تغییر دهد. این خودروساز eBoost را روی محبوب‌ترین خودروهای برقی خود مانند Blazer EV، Equinox EV، Cadillac Lyriq، و هوندا Prologue و Acura ZDX قرار داده است که با هوندا در یک سرمایه‌گذاری مشترک ساخته شده است. Cruise Origin - وسیله نقلیه خودکار الکتریکی هدفمند بدون فرمان یا پدال که جنرال موتورز در سال 2024 آن را رها کرد - از eBoost نیز استفاده کرد.
در یکی از تصادفات گزارش شده به NHTSA، راننده یک Lyriq مدل 2025 گفت که ترمزهای خود را در حالی که می خواستند خود را به پارکینگ روبروی فروشگاه بکشند از دست داده اند. به گفته راننده، خودرو از روی حاشیه عبور کرد و از جلوی فروشگاه تصادف کرد و به گفته راننده، «در وسط فروشگاه، در میان اثاثیه و ساختار فروشگاه» استراحت کرد.
در مورد دیگری، راننده یک بلیزر EV مدل 2024 گفت که آنها مجبور بودند "عمداً خودرو را به یک حاشیه سیمانی هدایت کنند" تا سرعت آن را کاهش دهند و از "تصادف فاجعه بار تقاطع" جلوگیری کنند.
این داستان با بیانیه ای از جنرال موتورز به روز شده است.

content_en:
Apple’s four-pack of second-generation AirTags is down to $79 (originally $99) at Amazon and at Target, which is the bundle’s lowest price yet. You can get an AirTag for $24 right now piecemeal, but getting four together as a set is a way to save even more. Why pay $96 for four when you can save $17? It felt like we had to wait longer for the cost to fall this much for first-gen AirTags, so it’s a little surprising to see the newer, better model available for less.
Apple’s four-pack of second-gen AirTags is $20 off
Big savings on the latest. We also found deals on Elgato’s biggest Stream Deck, a handy Switch 2 accessory, and more.
Big savings on the latest. We also found deals on Elgato’s biggest Stream Deck, a handy Switch 2 accessory, and more.
Apple AirTag (second-gen)
Apple’s latest AirTags features an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range.
The second-generation AirTag looks identical to the first-generation AirTag. All of its upgrades are inside, and primarily include spec improvements to let you more easily find it. It includes boosted speaker volume, longer range, and overall better tracking capabilities. My colleague Victoria Song had a much easier time tracking the latest AirTag on different floors compared to the older model. Read our review.
Some other great Verge-approved deals
- The biggest Stream Deck that Elgato makes is down to its lowest price since Amazon’s Prime Day in late June. Originally $249.99 for the gadget with 32 programmable keys, it’s $50 off at Amazon and Best Buy, totaling $199.99. Each key can be customized within Elgato’s desktop software for Windows or macOS, letting you set not just the command that executes when you press it, but also the imagery that displays on the key. You can assign simple functions to keys, like muting a mic or turning off a webcam. The integrations run deep, though, letting you create multi-button macros that run with a single button press.
- If you own a Switch 2 but still need a way to keep your original Switch’s Joy-Con recharged, there’s a great accessory that can charge Joy-Con for both systems and is half off at Amazon. Fastsnail’s charging dock that includes a USB-C-to-A cable and four Joy-Con charging sections is $6.99 (was already a great deal at $13.99) when you use the code NMSV9HX3, which the community at Slickdeals surfaced.
- Backbone’s One controller is one of the best ways to play games on your phone. It offers a comfortable, complete set of controls, whether you’re playing native phone games, or streaming console or PC games. Normally about $100, the Backbone One PlayStation Edition that works seamlessly on iOS with Sony’s Remote Play app is just $27 in used condition at eBay. The seller VIPOUTLET claims that the product is in “fair/good condition” and may have some blemishes, and it includes a 60-day warranty. You can purchase a one-year warranty via Allstate on eBay for an extra $4. It’s a good price if you’re curious but have been turned off by its retail price.

صرفه جویی بزرگ در آخرین. همچنین معاملاتی را در مورد بزرگترین عرشه جریان Elgato، لوازم جانبی Switch 2 و موارد دیگر پیدا کردیم.
صرفه جویی بزرگ در آخرین. همچنین معاملاتی را در مورد بزرگترین عرشه جریان Elgato، لوازم جانبی Switch 2 و موارد دیگر پیدا کردیم.

جدیدترین AirTags اپل دارای یک تراشه فوق‌باند ارتقا یافته برای ردیابی موقعیت مکانی دقیق‌تر، بلندگوی قابل توجهی بلندتر و محدوده بلوتوث گسترده‌تر است.
نسل دوم AirTag شبیه به AirTag نسل اول است. همه به‌روزرسانی‌های آن در داخل هستند و در درجه اول شامل بهبودهایی در مشخصات هستند تا به شما امکان می‌دهند راحت‌تر آن را پیدا کنید. این شامل افزایش صدای بلندگو، برد بلندتر و در کل قابلیت ردیابی بهتر است. ردیابی آخرین AirTag در طبقات مختلف در مقایسه با مدل قدیمی‌تر، همکار من ویکتوریا سانگ بسیار آسان‌تر بود. بررسی ما را بخوانید.
برخی دیگر از معاملات عالی تایید شده توسط Verge
- بزرگترین عرشه جریان الگاتو به پایین ترین قیمت خود از زمان پرایم روز آمازون در اواخر ژوئن رسیده است. در اصل 249.99 دلار برای این گجت با 32 کلید قابل برنامه ریزی، 50 دلار تخفیف در آمازون و Best Buy، در مجموع 199.99 دلار است. هر کلید را می توان در نرم افزار دسکتاپ Elgato برای ویندوز یا macOS سفارشی کرد و به شما این امکان را می دهد که نه تنها دستوری را که با فشار دادن آن اجرا می شود، بلکه تصاویری را که روی کلید نمایش داده می شود تنظیم کنید. می‌توانید عملکردهای ساده‌ای را به کلیدها اختصاص دهید، مانند خاموش کردن میکروفون یا خاموش کردن وب‌کم. با این حال، ادغام ها عمیق هستند و به شما امکان می دهند ماکروهای چند دکمه ای ایجاد کنید که با فشار دادن یک دکمه اجرا می شوند.
- اگر شما یک سوئیچ 2 دارید اما هنوز به راهی برای شارژ مجدد Joy-Con Switch اصلی خود نیاز دارید، یک وسیله جانبی عالی وجود دارد که می تواند Joy-Con را برای هر دو سیستم شارژ کند و در آمازون به نصف کاهش یافته است. پایه شارژ Fastsnail که شامل یک کابل USB-C-to-A و چهار بخش شارژ Joy-Con می‌شود، با استفاده از کد NMSV9HX3، که انجمن Slickdeals آن را منتشر کرد، 6.99 دلار است (که قبلاً قیمت بسیار خوبی بود و 13.99 دلار بود).
- کنترلر Backbone’s One یکی از بهترین راه ها برای انجام بازی در گوشی شما است. این یک مجموعه کامل و راحت از کنترل‌ها را ارائه می‌کند، چه در حال بازی کردن بازی‌های تلفنی بومی یا پخش جریانی کنسول یا بازی‌های رایانه شخصی باشید. به طور معمول حدود 100 دلار، نسخه Backbone One PlayStation که به طور یکپارچه روی iOS با برنامه Remote Play سونی کار می کند، فقط 27 دلار در شرایط استفاده شده در eBay قیمت دارد. فروشنده VIPOUTLET ادعا می کند که این محصول در شرایط "عادلانه/خوب" است و ممکن است دارای ایراداتی باشد و شامل 60 روز ضمانت می شود. شما می توانید یک سال گارانتی از طریق Allstate در eBay با 4 دلار اضافی خریداری کنید. اگر کنجکاو هستید اما قیمت خرده‌فروشی آن را از بین برده است، قیمت خوبی است.

content_en:
Today on Decoder, I’m talking with Tim Cadogan, the CEO of GoFundMe. You know GoFundMe — it’s a major fundraising platform where you can donate to help people with everything from medical expenses to Little League uniforms to starting a new business.
How GoFundMe became America’s backup plan
CEO Tim Cadogan on how a for-profit company becomes a social safety net.
Tim took over as CEO in March 2020 — a fascinating and chaotic moment in the United States, and the moment, you’ll hear me argue, I think GoFundMe became a load-bearing part of American culture.
Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here. Not a subscriber? You can sign up here.
It wasn’t just the pandemic that changed the nature of fundraising platforms like GoFundMe. 2020 was a major turning point in the history of political unrest in the US, and GoFundMe has become a central player in many contentious news events since — not just in the US, but all over the world.
The platform is also now a kind of proxy for the broken healthcare system — medical expenses are the most popular category of fundraising on GoFundMe. You might be surprised to hear Tim say this is not just in America, but in every market GoFundMe operates in.
All of this means GoFundMe sits inside a ton of big, messy ideas: wealth distribution, geopolitical conflict, the holes in the social safety net. And that’s also in direct tension with the platform being a for-profit company, collecting fees and tips and feeling the pressure to grow as a business.
So you can imagine I had a lot of questions for Tim: how he thinks about all this, and how he makes some very tough decisions about what money to make and what money not to make. To his credit, he was game to go there and talked about it all pretty openly.
Okay: Tim Cadogan, CEO of GoFundMe. Here we go.
This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
Tim Cadogan, you’re the CEO of GoFundMe. Welcome to Decoder.
Hey, thank you very much for having me, Nilay.
I am very excited to talk to you. GoFundMe occupies an incredibly unique place, I think, in our culture, particularly in American culture and American society. It’s a for-profit company, and I have a lot of questions about how you think about its place in our culture and the need to grow and deliver returns.
I was also doing the research. You joined this company in the pandemic, in the heart of the pandemic, when it felt like everything changed. Now, we’re six years later; maybe things have settled, maybe they haven’t.
But I actually just want to start there. You became the CEO when the idea that the public health system — how we think about healthcare in America — got flipped upside down. I know that healthcare expenses are, I think, the single biggest category on GoFundMe. How do you think about the platform, and how do you think about that path from 2020 to now?
Well, yes, there’s a lot in there. So I started on March the 2nd, 2020, which was about a week before it became very clear in the US that the pandemic was going to have major implications, but it was already becoming clear in other parts of the world.
We operate in 20 countries, and we did back then. For instance, Italy is an important country for us, and that was probably the first European country that experienced a big impact. So it was just becoming evident; in fact, by the end of the first week, we went remote. Things came at us, all of us in the world, very quickly. It certainly came very quickly for me, trying to figure out a new company, a new space, and all this stuff happening.
The root of what we do is extremely simple. We help people help each other. And we are there to help people in whatever situation they need help. Sometimes those are the most consequential, the most significant thing that is happening in someone’s life and has ever happened in their life. And sometimes they’re very lighthearted and fun and forward-looking, like going to college or sending your kids’ sports team on tour because they’ve made the state championships, you name it. Everything in between: if someone thinks they need help, we’re here to help them mobilize support from friends, family, and networks.
So when you talk about the pandemic, that is a time when millions of people needed a lot of help. In some cases, for medical situations and everything related to that, some cases because they weren’t able to work anymore. Or we had a phenomenon that was not expected — and we could not have anticipated this — when hundreds of thousands of small businesses were shutting down: restaurants, bars, music venues. They were all having to shut down for a while and didn’t know how long they had to furlough employees.
We had tens of thousands of fundraisers that were often being set up by really loyal customers who said, “I love my local restaurant. I really feel bad for the wait staff and the kitchen staff. I want to set up a GoFundMe for them.” And we had so many of those, and it was such a different use case that it was a struggle to figure out how we handle the volume.
For example, when you raise money into a fundraiser, to take the money out, you have to go through a [know your customer] process to verify that you’re the right person. If you’re a business, you have to go through a KYB process. And that’s different and more complicated. It means you need paperwork. And if people are no longer at their place of business, how do you get the paperwork?
So, we and our payment processors who we work with — all money goes through our third-party payment processors, not through us — had to figure out how to get through this huge amount of new fundraisers to navigate the situation. Those are a couple of examples of this kind of thing, but it goes back to helping people help each other in whatever situation they’re dealing with.
I think the reason I wanted to start there, and you can disagree with me on this, is because that feels, to me, like...

title_en: Hugging Face reportedly in talks to be acquired for $13B
title_fa: Hugging Face reportedly in talks to be acquired for $13B
excerpt_en: Hugging Face has reportedly been fielding acquisition offers that would value the company at around $13B. But with the founders' feeling of responsibility to community, doubts arise as to whether a sale will happen.
excerpt_fa: Hugging Face has reportedly been fielding acquisition offers that would value the company at around $13B. But with the founders' feeling of responsibility to community, doubts arise as to whether a sale will happen.
content_en:
Hugging Face has been approached to sell at a valuation of $13 billion or more, Business Insider reported over the weekend.
The startup’s platform and open source community is where developers and researchers share, find, test, and deploy AI models. Hugging Face was recently the target of an attack from one of OpenAI’s systems, which broke out of its sandbox during a cybersecurity evaluation and breached the startup’s servers.
It’s not clear who Hugging Face has been in talks with, and no deal has yet been reached, according to Business Insider. However, the startup has reportedly been talking to banks to help evaluate bids.
The talks come amid increased interest in companies providing core AI infrastructure services, as evidenced by Stripe’s $7 billion acquisition of OpenRouter.
Hugging Face last raised in 2023 at a $4.5 billion post-money valuation in a round led by Salesforce Ventures, with participation from Alphabet, GV, IBM Ventures, and others.
On a recent episode of the TechCrunch Equity podcast, Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said that the company was “close to profitability” and only “recently started to touch the money that [it] raised three years ago,” adding that the startup is thinking about how to optimize for “long-term sustainability of the company rather than short-term profits or fundraising maximization.”
“We’re more in a unique position where we can keep creating value for the community and for AI builders,” he said.
The way Delangue has discussed the company’s responsibility to the Hugging Face community raises questions over whether the startup is truly considering selling or is simply fielding offers for what has become a central pillar in AI infrastructure.
“We’re building a platform for the community, and they’re trusting us with sharing their data and their models on the platform, so we have a long-term responsibility to them,” Delangue said on Equity.
More to the point, the company earlier this year turned down a $500 million investment from Nvidia that would have valued it at $7 billion, saying at the time that it didn’t want a single dominant investor to sway decisions.
TechCrunch has reached out to Hugging Face for more information.

title_en: Netflix reportedly considers opening its app to other streamers
title_fa: Netflix reportedly considers opening its app to other streamers
excerpt_en: Netflix executives have considered making third-party streaming services available within its app, according to a report from The New York Times. The recent discussions reportedly centered around bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix, though it's unclear whether the streaming...
excerpt_fa: Netflix executives have considered making third-party streaming services available within its app, according to a report from The New York Times. The recent discussions reportedly centered around bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix, though it's unclear whether the streaming...
content_en:
Netflix executives have considered making third-party streaming services available within its app, according to a report from The New York Times. The recent discussions reportedly centered around bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix, though it’s unclear whether the streaming giant would sell subscriptions to the other services or add their content to its app.
Netflix reportedly considers opening its app to other streamers
Executives discussed making Peacock and Fox One available through the Netflix app, The New York Times reports.
Executives discussed making Peacock and Fox One available through the Netflix app, The New York Times reports.
While Amazon’s Prime Video and Roku have long sold subscriptions to rival services, the move would be a major change for Netflix, which has only joined bundles with other streamers. YouTube — Netflix’s biggest rival — will also include access to Peacock as part of its Premium subscription next year.
Netflix currently has no “imminent deal” planned, The New York Times reports.
But Netflix has already begun dabbling in third-party streaming partnerships in France, where it folded live channels and streaming content from local broadcaster TF1 into its app in June. When asked about this partnership during a July earnings call, Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters said the company is seeing “promising” results. “If we see additional deals that similarly serve our members that work for our partner, that work for us, we’ll certainly consider them,” Peters said. Netflix declined to comment.
Update, August 24th: Added Netflix’s response.

title_en: US nutrition startup Berry Street merges with India’s Healthify as GLP-1 trends upwards
title_fa: US nutrition startup Berry Street merges with India’s Healthify as GLP-1 trends upwards
excerpt_en: Berry Street founder Noah Kotlove and Healthify founder Tushar Vashisht will act as co-CEOs of the new entity.
excerpt_fa: Berry Street founder Noah Kotlove and Healthify founder Tushar Vashisht will act as co-CEOs of the new entity.
content_en:
U.S. nutrition startup Berry Street said on Monday it has merged with Khosla Ventures-backed Indian startup Healthify to bank on the popular trend of people turning to GLP-1 drugs to lose weight.
The companies didn’t disclose the financial details of the deal. A report from JP Morgan published this year suggested that over 30 million people in the U.S. will be on GLP-1 by 2030.
The companies said Berry Street founder Noah Kotlove and Healthify founder Tushar Vashisht will act as co-CEOs of the new entity. In the U.S., the company will operate under the Berry Street banner, and in other markets like India, it will operate under the Healthify brand.
Healthify, which has raised over $150 million in funding, per Crunchbase, offers both AI-powered and human fitness and nutritional coaching via an app. Last year, the company expanded its operations in the U.S., and also started offering GLP-1-aided programs in India. The startup claims it has so far served more than 45 million customers.
“Healthify’s mission has been to put a dietitian in every human’s pocket. We have spent a decade proving that AI can drive life-changing outcomes at scale. Berry Street gives us the clinical backbone and the coverage infrastructure to deliver that promise to the U.S. market at a scale no one has achieved before,” Healthify’s CEO Vashisht said in a press release.
Berry Street has a network of over 2,000 clinics and offers insurance-covered GLP-1 care. The company last year raised $50 million in a fundraising round from Northzone, Sofina, and FJ Labs. This startup also provides AI-powered nutrition coaching and meal tracking, and claims it has served over 200,000 people in collaboration with Amazon, Walmart, and other platforms.
“By pairing AI with a nationwide network of expert clinicians, Healthify and Berry Street are building the platform that will redefine metabolic care, giving everyone access to daily nutrition guidance and expert dietitian advice,” Khosla Ventures’ founder Vinod Khosla said in a statement.

title_en: The biggest downsides to using a digital car key
title_fa: The biggest downsides to using a digital car key
excerpt_en: Many newer vehicles can be accessed from the owner's phone, if they've set it up. There are some things to consider before adding your key.
excerpt_fa: Many newer vehicles can be accessed from the owner's phone, if they've set it up. There are some things to consider before adding your key.
content_en:
The biggest downsides to using a digital car key
You can use your phone to access your car -- but should you?
Digital car keys are so convenient. You can lock and unlock your vehicle from your phone instead of fumbling with a physical key or even a key fob. But like every technology advancement that touts convenience, they also come with risks. In many cases, these risks can be mitigated once you have a better understanding of how digital keys work and take the proper precautions.
Digital car keys are available for Android and iOS phones; Samsung even has its own digital key technology that works with select vehicles. With compatible Android and iPhone devices and vehicles, you can use Google Wallet or Apple Wallet, respectively, to not only lock and unlock the vehicle but, with some cars, start it as well. The technology is built around criteria set by the Car Connectivity Consortium, which devised the standard for digital keys way back in 2018.
There's no denying how easy digital car keys are to use and even share with others. But there are concerns. For example, what if your phone dies, malfunctions or is lost? Can you still get into and start your vehicle? It's important to understand these concerns around digital car keys.
What to consider when using a digital car key
Digital car keys are not at risk for relay attacks like key fobs, whereby a thief amplifies the fob's signal to unlock the car without even having the fob in their possession. Instead, digital keys use ultra-wideband (UWB) or near-field communication (NFC) to communicate with your vehicle, so the car won't unlock unless your phone is actually nearby. But they aren't completely immune to attacks. If your phone is stolen and someone gets hold of it, this means they might be able to gain access to your vehicle. That said, most car makers include additional levels of authorization to help prevent thieves or even your underage kids from being able to access the car.
The best defense against this is to keep your phone as secure as possible with two-factor authentication, secure passwords and remote wiping capability in the event of loss or theft. There may also be an option to use a second device to suspend the digital key until you locate your phone. With iPhone, for example, all you need to do is mark your device as lost, and Apple CarKey will automatically lock down the app.
Another common concern is that scary scenario when your phone dies. It's bad enough not to be able to hail an Uber or call home, but what if this means you can't even get into your car? Thankfully, that isn't the case. Just as most key fobs have a hidden physical key or a secondary option to start your car if the battery dies, digital keys have failsafe options. With both Apple and Android, many keys and cards can work up to five hours after your device battery dies, using reserve power via NFC. There are concerns as well that Bluetooth or NFC technology might not be working, but it's unlikely. It's slightly more probable that the app could crash, freeze or require an update at the worst possible time. The company's cloud server could also go offline, though most big companies have backup servers just in case. None of these scenarios are common, but it's good to know what's possible.
Digital keys are the future
Just as so many other technologies are going digital, from wallets to door locks, digital car keys are the future. That said, it's always a good idea to have a backup. Keep the key fob with you anyway, or safely at home so someone can get it to you in the event of an emergency.
But provided you keep your phone sufficiently charged and the app updated, using digital keys should be easy as pie. Sure, things can always go wrong with digital technology. But with the right precautions and a backup plan in place, you'll be able to use your digital car keys daily without issue.

title_en: The best way to test your Dolby Atmos sound system
title_fa: The best way to test your Dolby Atmos sound system
excerpt_en: When you're testing your Dolby Atmos system, pick a good benchmark video and stick with it.
excerpt_fa: When you're testing your Dolby Atmos system, pick a good benchmark video and stick with it.
content_en:
The best way to test your Dolby Atmos sound system
Pick a good benchmark video, and stick with it.
Immersive, cinema-grade audio at home isn't impossible, but getting it right can be a labor of love. Setting up a Dolby Atmos sound system, for instance, requires careful speaker placement and plenty of fine-tuning for the best results. If it's done right, the audio should feel like it's coming from all around you.
The only problem is knowing how to test it, because you can't just hook it up and assume everything will sound right in your room. Once you've checked each speaker is working properly, you'll need to put the entire system through its paces to check that you're getting the full Dolby Atmos experience.
Test each speaker with the official Dolby Atmos test file
You've installed your Dolby Atmos sound system. Before you settle down for a movie, you're going to want to perform some technical testing first. To be clear, this isn't going to be a test of how good your system sounds. It isn't necessarily calibrated, and you'll probably need to make further tweaks and changes.
What it is, however, is a test run of each component in your Atmos setup. Dolby's official 7.1.4 channel test file lets you test whether each speaker and audio channel is working as expected. This'll let you check your speakers are working properly, with clean audio and no dropouts. It can also be used with smaller Atmos setups, such as 5.1.2, although the test includes channels that those systems don't have. Those channels may just stay silent, or it may sound like it's coming from a different speaker than the file suggests, depending on your config.
It's also an immersion test. If your setup is working correctly, each test signal will match to a specific speaker and correspond to a different audio channel. As the channel test works through each speaker, you should be able to pinpoint where it's coming from, matching up to what the test file is telling you. For instance, if the speaker tells you that it's playing from the left top rear, it should sound like it's coming from there.
The test file is a video, so you'll see a visual guide to explain which speaker should be sounding. If you've placed a speaker in the wrong place, this'll give you a chance to swap it out. You can also correct any wrongly-assigned channels to speakers in your settings, if needed.
The official Dolby Atmos 7.1.4 channel test file is available to download from Dolby's website. Third-party alternatives also exist online with different audio mixes to try out, too. Once you've tested the setup and you're confident that it's technically working, you can move onto trying it out with some real content.
Use a short movie or song as a benchmark to stress test your setup
At this point, each speaker should be working, so the next test is to try playing real content you'd listen to that has been mixed for Dolby Atmos. You'll only know from playing real content, like movies you watch or songs you listen to, if the immersive experience you're expecting is right or not.
You can sit for a full-length movie but, realistically, that isn't a good test. You'll want a brief sequence that you can watch and replay, repeatedly, while you make adjustments. It'll give you a benchmark to refer back to with each change you make. Once you have that, you can make adjustments to your setup to improve the audio.
Sol Levante is a short anime film produced by Netflix that's perfect for this. It's under five minutes long, so you can replay it again and again. More importantly, it makes use of an extensive Dolby Atmos spatial audio mix that works as a stress test for your setup. The audio playback features movements and positional effects to help you test how accurately your system places sounds around and above you.
There are a couple of things you'll want to listen out for as the movie plays. Volume is important, but for Dolby Atmos, spatial awareness is the greater priority. Audio that moves around on-screen should move throughout your speakers, with dialogue that stays anchored and clear at the front. Any ambient effects should help give you that immersive feel of a space greater than just the screen, filling the entire room around you from top to bottom.
The whole point of Dolby Atmos audio is for you to feel like you're experiencing three-dimensional audio. If Sol Levante sounds right, you can move onto a bigger test, like a full-blown movie. Just be sure that you stick to a benchmark if you want to make further tweaks. It could be a key point in the film with a few minutes of variation in the audio, for instance, that you replay again and again to get your setup sounding right.
You can also use other types of content, like music through Apple Music, to test Dolby Atmos. For the full Dolby Atmos experience, however, you'll need an Apple TV 4K connected via HDMI to your kit. The important thing here is picking songs with obvious spatial effects, with a good set of vocals, instruments and effects throughout. It helps if it's music that you listen to regularly, as you'll have a better feel for how the music should sound in your room.
Double-check your settings and connections
Your Dolby Atmos setup should sound clear and well calibrated by this point. If it doesn't, there are several points in the chain that you can double check to fix any problems.
The source might be the issue itself. Make sure that the movie or song that you're playing is made for Dolby Atmos, meaning it has Dolby Atmos audio available for playback, rather than standard 5.1 surround or stereo. The streaming service you're watching and the playback device itself need to support Atmos content, too.
It's never a bad idea to double-check all of your connections, either. Start with your individual speakers and subwoofer, but also check the link between your playback devices and your sound system. HDMI ARC or eARC is probably the right call here, as it lets your TV pass Dolby Atmos audio through to your sound...

title_en: What's the difference between Dolby Digital 5.1 and Dolby Digital Plus?
title_fa: تفاوت بین Dolby Digital 5.1 و Dolby Digital Plus چیست؟
excerpt_en: Is one better than the other? Will your equipment support both? Here's what you need to know and how it might affect your setup.
excerpt_fa: Is one better than the other? Will your equipment support both? Here's what you need to know and how it might affect your setup.
content_en:
What's the difference between Dolby Digital 5.1 and Dolby Digital Plus?
These naming conventions are getting out of hand.
The names make the difference sound simple: Dolby Digital 5.1 is regular surround sound, while Dolby Digital Plus must be the better version. The actual difference isn't quite that simple. Dolby Digital is the older format and tops out at 5.1 channels, while Dolby Digital Plus can carry 5.1 or 7.1 surround sound and can also deliver Dolby Atmos. That makes DD+ more capable, but the "Plus" doesn't guarantee more channels or better sound every time.
Dolby Digital tops out at 5.1 surround sound
First, it helps to decode the number. A channel is essentially a separate audio feed assigned to a particular speaker position. In a 5.1 surround sound system, the five main channels cover the front left, center, front right, left surround and right surround positions. The ".1" refers to a separate low-frequency effects channel, usually handled by a subwoofer for things like explosions and other deep bass.
Dolby Digital, which you may also see labeled AC-3, can carry anything from mono sound up to that full 5.1 configuration. It became closely associated with DVDs, digital television and earlier generations of home-theater equipment. Like Dolby Digital Plus, it uses lossy compression, which reduces file size by discarding some audio information.
Dolby Digital Plus can carry 7.1 and Dolby Atmos
Dolby Digital Plus, also called E-AC-3, still uses lossy compression but supports up to 7.1 channels. A 7.1 soundtrack adds two more surround channels beyond the conventional 5.1 layout, typically giving the system more separation around and behind the listener. The important word is can: DD+ also supports ordinary 5.1 audio, so seeing the newer format doesn't automatically mean more channels are being used. In other words, a Dolby Digital Plus logo isn't an instruction to go shopping for two more speakers.
The newer format becomes particularly useful for streaming. Dolby designed Digital Plus for streaming, on-demand and downloaded content, and services such as Netflix use it for multichannel audio. Its combination of surround-sound support and compression makes it well suited to delivering that audio over the internet.
Dolby Digital Plus can also carry Dolby Atmos. Atmos goes beyond assigning every sound to a fixed speaker channel by including information about where sounds should be positioned around the listener, allowing compatible equipment to adapt the soundtrack to the speaker setup.
That doesn't make Dolby Atmos and Dolby Digital Plus the same thing. Streaming services can use Dolby Digital Plus to deliver Atmos, while Blu-ray discs can instead pair Atmos with Dolby TrueHD, a separate lossless format that preserves the audio data rather than discarding some of it during compression.
Should you use Dolby Digital or Dolby Digital Plus?
If your TV, streamer and audio equipment all support Dolby Digital Plus, DD+ is generally the better setting to leave enabled. It can carry a regular 5.1 soundtrack just fine while leaving room for 7.1 or Dolby Atmos when the source offers them. You don't need to choose standard Dolby Digital simply because you have a 5.1 speaker system.
Older equipment is where Dolby Digital is still the safer choice. DD+ content can be converted into standard Dolby Digital so older systems can play it, but an older Dolby Digital decoder can't read the newer DD+ bitstream directly. For that to work, a compatible device such as your TV, streaming box or Blu-ray player needs to convert the DD+ audio to standard Dolby Digital before sending it to the older equipment.
So if your equipment supports both, leave Dolby Digital Plus enabled. Switch to Dolby Digital when compatibility with older hardware requires it.

title_en: The new Shokz OpenFit Air 2 earbuds are nearly 20 percent lighter than the previous generation
title_fa: The new Shokz OpenFit Air 2 earbuds are nearly 20 percent lighter than the previous generation
excerpt_en: They feature an open-ear design that reduces pressure and heat buildup.
excerpt_fa: They feature an open-ear design that reduces pressure and heat buildup.
content_en:
The new Shokz OpenFit Air 2 earbuds are nearly 20 percent lighter than the previous generation
They feature an open-ear design that reduces pressure and heat buildup.
Shokz just introduced the OpenFit Air 2 earbuds, a refresh of the original model. These earbuds are around 17 percent lighter than the previous version, clocking in at 7.2g per unit. That's around the same weight as a handful of paperclips.
This is an open-ear design, which delivers a couple of benefits. First of all, there's no ear canal pressure, as the earbuds don't create a seal of any kind. The design also gives users quicker access to their surroundings, making them a decent choice for exercising outside in a busy city. As a matter of fact, the standard Shokz OpenAir 2 earbuds easily made our list of the best headphones for running.
The only potential downside to this form factor is that they connect via an ear-hook. The ergonomic design ensures long-term comfort, with a caveat. These ear-hooks could get in the way of glasses and certain hats. Take a look at photos and decide for yourself.
Otherwise, the company promises "richer bass" and "fuller sound." The earbuds use the company's proprietary Bassphere audio driver and its OpenBass 2.0 algorithm. There's an angled speaker that directs audio toward the ear for a "more natural listening experience" and an app with access to four preset EQ modes and two custom EQ profiles.
The OpenFit Air 2 earbuds last eight hours per charge, with up to 36 hours of use when considering the included charging case. They also offer a 10-minute quick charge that gives three hours of playback. This model integrates with Bluetooth 6.1 and allows for multipoint connections. They will be available to purchase on August 27 for $130.
Shokz also just introduced the OpenRun Air 2 earbuds, which feature a design that wraps around the back of the head. These are also lighter than the previous iteration, with an overall form factor that prioritizes stability and minimizes bounce. After all, these are for runners.
They use a bone conduction driver and also connect to the company's app for EQ adjustments. The battery lasts ten hours on a single charge, with a five-minute quick charge for two hours of playback. The OpenRun Air 2 earbuds are also available on August 27 and, lo and behold, also cost $130.

title_en: Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
title_fa: Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
excerpt_en: Even though the US has relaxed its restrictions of AI chip exports to China, illegal exports are apparently still taking place.
excerpt_fa: Even though the US has relaxed its restrictions of AI chip exports to China, illegal exports are apparently still taking place.
content_en:
Taiwan reportedly indicted NVIDIA employees for exporting prohibited AI servers to China
The nine individuals are accused of 'severely damaged our nation's image,' prosecutors said.
Although the US has relaxed its restrictions on NVIDIA AI chip exports to China, illegal exports apparently still take place. Prosecutors in Taiwan just indicted nine individuals, including NVIDIA and Super Micro employees, for illegally bringing AI servers into China, Reuters reported.
The defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image," prosecutors from the northern city of Keelung said in a statement. They did this, the team added, despite being "fully aware" of NVIDIA and Super Micro's "rigorous" export control procedures.
Although NVIDIA is an American company, most of its chips are manufactured by the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest chip maker by far. TSMC's latest Blackwell AI chips are manufactured in Phoenix, Arizona, but are still shipped to Taiwan for advanced packaging prior to final assembly.
The US has banned the sale of cutting-edge AI tech from NVIDIA and others to China since 2022. Recently, it has allowed sales to China of previous-generation products like H200 chips that are several years old. Taiwan is ultra-strict about exports of newer technology, lest it displease US regulators and, in particular, the Trump administration.
Despite Taiwan's clampdown, bad actors have found ways to get such chips into China. In one instance, $1 billion worth of server racks may have been shipped through Southeast Asian countries like Thailand or Malaysia to circumvent US export controls. In another case, the US charged three people with allegedly exporting $3.5 billion worth of AI servers to China, again by routing them through third-party countries.
content_fa:
طبق گزارش ها، تایوان کارمندان NVIDIA را به دلیل صادرات سرورهای ممنوعه هوش مصنوعی به چین متهم کرده است
دادستان ها گفتند که این 9 نفر متهم هستند که به شدت به وجهه کشور ما آسیب رسانده اند.
اگرچه ایالات متحده محدودیت های خود را بر صادرات تراشه های NVIDIA AI به چین کاهش داده است، ظاهراً صادرات غیرقانونی همچنان ادامه دارد. به گزارش رویترز، دادستان های تایوان به تازگی ۹ نفر از جمله کارمندان NVIDIA و Super Micro را به دلیل ورود غیرقانونی سرورهای هوش مصنوعی به چین متهم کردند.
دادستان های شهر شمالی کیلونگ در بیانیه ای گفتند: متهمان "در سطوح مختلف برای سود هنگفت، صادرات غیرقانونی سرورهای پیشرفته، افزایش هزینه های انطباق شرکت ها، و آسیب جدی به وجهه بین المللی کشورمان، با یکدیگر تبانی کردند." تیم افزود، علیرغم آگاهی کامل از رویه‌های کنترل صادرات «سخت‌انگیز» NVIDIA و Super Micro، آنها این کار را انجام دادند.
اگرچه انویدیا یک شرکت آمریکایی است، اما بیشتر تراشه های آن توسط شرکت تولید نیمه هادی تایوان (TSMC)، بزرگترین سازنده تراشه در جهان، تولید می شود. آخرین تراشه‌های هوش مصنوعی بلک‌ول TSMC در فینیکس، آریزونا تولید می‌شوند، اما همچنان برای بسته‌بندی پیشرفته قبل از مونتاژ نهایی به تایوان ارسال می‌شوند.
ایالات متحده از سال 2022 فروش فناوری پیشرفته هوش مصنوعی از NVIDIA و سایرین به چین را ممنوع کرده است. اخیراً این کشور اجازه فروش محصولات نسل قبلی مانند تراشه های H200 را به چین داده است که چندین سال قدمت دارند. تایوان در مورد صادرات فناوری جدیدتر سختگیرانه عمل می کند تا مبادا تنظیم کننده های ایالات متحده و به ویژه دولت ترامپ را ناراضی کند.
علی‌رغم سرکوب تایوان، بازیگران بد راه‌هایی برای وارد کردن چنین تراشه‌هایی به چین پیدا کرده‌اند. در یک نمونه، یک میلیارد دلار رک سرور ممکن است از طریق کشورهای آسیای جنوب شرقی مانند تایلند یا مالزی برای دور زدن کنترل صادرات ایالات متحده ارسال شده باشد. در یک مورد دیگر، ایالات متحده سه نفر را متهم کرد که ادعا می‌شود 3.5 میلیارد دلار سرورهای هوش مصنوعی به چین صادر کرده‌اند و دوباره آنها را از طریق کشورهای شخص ثالث هدایت کرده‌اند.

title_en: What is a VESA mount and how to know what type your TV has
title_fa: What is a VESA mount and how to know what type your TV has
excerpt_en: Those 200 × 200 and 400 × 400 numbers tell you where the mounting holes line up, but you still need to check the mount's weight limit and hardware.
excerpt_fa: Those 200 × 200 and 400 × 400 numbers tell you where the mounting holes line up, but you still need to check the mount's weight limit and hardware.
content_en:
What is a VESA mount and how to know what type your TV has
The VESA dimensions tell you where the mounting holes line up, but you still need to check the mount's weight limit and hardware.
Thankfully, VESA 400 × 400 isn't another TV resolution you need to learn. VESA stands for Video Electronics Standards Association, and in TV-mount shopping, a VESA size or VESA pattern describes the spacing between the mounting holes on the back of a TV or display. A VESA mount isn't one particular style of bracket; it simply supports one or more of those standardized patterns.
What does a VESA size such as 200 × 200 mean?
Look at the back of a typical mountable TV and you'll find threaded mounting holes, usually arranged in a square or rectangle. The VESA pattern describes the distance between those holes, measured in millimeters.
The first number is the horizontal distance and the second is the vertical distance. So a TV with a 400 × 200 pattern has mounting holes spaced 400mm apart from left to right and 200mm apart from top to bottom. A 200 × 200 pattern measures 200mm in both directions.
The VESA numbers don't describe the TV's resolution or screen dimensions. Larger TVs often use larger mounting patterns, but screen size alone doesn't tell you which pattern a particular model uses. Checking your exact TV model is more reliable than guessing from its screen size.
You also don't need a mount limited to that exact VESA size. Many mounts support multiple VESA patterns, so you don't need a bracket labeled only for your exact size. Your TV's pattern just needs to appear on the mount's list of supported patterns.
How to find your TV's VESA pattern
The easiest method doesn't require a ruler at all. Look up the exact TV model in its manual or on the manufacturer's support page and find the wall-mount or VESA specifications. Manufacturers commonly list the mounting-hole pattern in millimeters.
If you can't find the specification, you can measure the mounting holes yourself. Measure from the center of one mounting hole to the center of the corresponding hole horizontally, then do the same vertically. Write the result as horizontal × vertical, in millimeters.
For example, if the mounting holes are 400mm apart horizontally and 200mm apart vertically, the TV has a 400 × 200 VESA pattern. Measure in millimeters so you can compare the result directly with the mount's specifications.
A matching VESA pattern isn't enough
A matching VESA pattern tells you the bracket can line up with the TV's mounting holes. It doesn't tell you whether the mount can safely hold the TV, so the next specification to check is its weight limit.
Compare the mount's maximum load with the weight of your TV. A bracket can support the correct VESA pattern and still be unsuitable for a TV that's too heavy.
You should also check the hardware required by your TV. VESA compatibility also says nothing about how the bracket should attach to the wall. Once you've confirmed the pattern and weight rating, use the TV manufacturer's instructions to check the required mounting screws and follow the mount manufacturer's instructions for attaching the bracket to the wall.
